fr_renault_d2: The Char D2 was an interwar French medium tank, worked up from the Char D1 into a more advanced design and seen as a substitute for the Char B1 heavy tank, which a proposed League of Nations limit of 20 tonnes on armoured vehicles threatened to outlaw. In the game it suits a supporting role: the gun penetrates best at closer ranges, but even angled, the armour cannot make the front immune, so it should fight from near cover and avoid being caught in the open or swarmed. It arrived in the "Starfighters" update.
fr_renault_r39: France's most numerous tank when the Second World War began, with 900 in service, the R.35 was built for infantry support and fought other tanks poorly; only some received the SA 38 gun, as the H.35 and H.39 had priority. In the game it plays like other early French light tanks, giving up speed for thick armour and a low silhouette. Its gun is reasonable but does little harm once it penetrates and reloads slowly, and the commander works alone in a one-man turret. It was added as the R.39 in Update 1.75 "La Résistance" and renamed in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
fr_saint_chamond: France's second tank of the First World War grew out of a business feud: when Schneider would not share its patents for free, FAMH designed a rival on a modified Holt tractor chassis. Fielded in 1917, it tended to dig its long nose into trenches and was retired after the war; one running example survives at the Musée des Blindés. In the game it is huge, slow and only proof against small arms, with a cramped crew layout and a 75 mm gun that has almost no arc of fire, yet the Mle 1897 still hurts newer tanks. It was a 2025 "The Great War!" event reward in Update "Hornet's Sting".
fr_samp_t_fcs: This is the radar vehicle of the SAMP/T "Mamba", a truck-mounted, medium-range air defence system that the Franco-Italian Eurosam consortium built around the Aster 30 missile in the early 2010s; France later cut its order from twelve systems to ten. In the game it works with two launcher vehicles, and its ARABEL radar can see targets 80 km away and track ten at a time. It has no weapons and no protection, and destroying it puts the whole complex out of action, so its large bulk needs careful hiding. It arrived in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
fr_samp_t_launcher: One of two truck-mounted launchers in France's SAMP/T "Mamba", the Eurosam system that took the naval Aster 30 missile onto land in the early 2010s. In the game the launchers come with the TADS radar vehicle and need no separate research, and their Aster 30s combine active radar homing with inertial guidance and a datalink, and they are agile enough to catch targets at long range. The trucks cannot fire at ground targets and have no armour, so their large size has to be kept behind cover. It was added with the rest of the system in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
fr_sk105_a2: This SK-105A2 Kürassier is a light tank built around a 105 mm CN105G1 gun with an autoloader that reloads in about four seconds. That fast-firing gun, along with a low profile and good mobility, makes it a strong long-range shooter from raised positions near cover, while it fares badly in head-on or close-range fights, so flanking and sniping suit it far better than charging into the main fight. It was added to the game in Update "Ixwa Strike".
fr_somua_s35: SOMUA's 1935 cavalry tank was agile for its day and well protected by sloped, mostly cast armour up to 47 mm thick, though that made it costly to build and maintain; like the Char B1, it left the commander to aim, load and fire the 47 mm SA35 gun alone. In the game it is a support tank rather than a spearhead: its gun is adequate by French standards at its rank, but penetration drops sharply with range, reloads are slow, damage after penetrating is poor, and light tanks can easily outmanoeuvre it. It came with Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_somua_sau40: Developed by SOMUA alongside the S.35 between 1935 and 1937, the SAu 40 mounted a 75 mm gun in a reworked hull to support heavier French tanks; the prototype was completed in 1939 after delays with the gun, and it is unclear whether more were built or fought. In the game it reuses much of the S.35, including a roughly 40 mm cast hull, but its APHE shell, rare in the French tree, makes one-shot kills likely. It is slow and tall, and its prominent commander's cupola is an easy weak spot to target. It was added in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_somua_sm: SOMUA's rival to the AMX-50 in a post-war heavy tank contest was ordered in 1946, but the 56-tonne prototype arrived only in October 1951, still without an engine, and was not tested until 1953; the project was cancelled and the sole example scrapped. In the game it shares the autoloading 100 mm SA47 L/58 and similar mobility with the Lorraine 40t and AMX-50 (TOA100), but its hull and upper turret front stop most APCBC and some APDS, and its ready rack is a little larger, so it can be played more aggressively. It was released as a store premium in Update "Raining Fire".
fr_tpk_641_vpc: The TPK 6.41 was a convoy-escort anti-aircraft prototype that put twin 20 mm Oerlikon KAD cannons in a GAI-D01 mount on ACMAT's VLRA, a cheap and simple utility chassis built since 1965 and used for more than 75 models; it never entered production. In the game it is very mobile, and its fast-firing pair of cannons threatens both aircraft and lightly armoured vehicles, but it has almost no armour and the guns depress poorly, with the driver's cab restricting fire to the front. It came to the game in Update 2.33 "Air Superiority".
fr_vab_santal: The SANTAL is a late-1980s air defence version of the French VAB armoured personnel carrier, armed with the Mistral surface-to-air missile, which was integrated in 1987 to shield ground troops from helicopters and low-flying aircraft. The VAB's modular layout also produced relatives such as the MEPHISTO tank destroyer. In the game it pairs an agile armoured hull with Mistral missiles that engage aircraft quickly and accurately, making it a flexible anti-aircraft option. It arrived in Update "Fire and Ice".
fr_vbci: The VBCI came out of a 1990s modular wheeled vehicle programme to replace France's AMX-10P; Britain and Germany took part until requirements diverged, and France carried on alone. The first 200 entered service in June 2010, and 630 of the 25 mm-armed infantry fighting vehicles had been built when production ended in 2018. In the game it pairs speed with a strong 25 mm cannon, thermal optics and laser warning, while thin armour, a bulky hull and a wheelbase that hampers manoeuvring are its weak points. It was added in Update 2.43 "Storm Warning".
fr_vbci2_mct30: Nexter developed the VBCI-2 as an export successor to the original VBCI, and its defining feature is the MCT30 turret, which pairs a 30 mm autocannon with secondary weapons and can engage both ground and air targets. In the game a stabilised gun and modern fire control let it shoot accurately whether moving or halted, while thermal imaging and a laser warning system help it find targets and react to threats. Its armour is intended to keep out light and medium-calibre fire. It arrived in Update "La Royale".
fr_vcac_mephisto: MEPHISTO, short for Module Élévateur Panoramique Hot Installé Sur Tourelle Orientable, is a French anti-tank system from the 1970s, with prototypes appearing around 1978, that combines HOT guided missiles with a raised panoramic sight on a rotating, unmanned turret. In the game the HOT missiles let it destroy armour from a safe distance, the elevated sight gives it a wide view for identifying targets, and the turret can traverse to meet threats from any direction. The same module can be fitted to other vehicles such as the SANTAL. It was introduced in Update "Danger Zone".
fr_vextra_105: GIAT built the Vextra prototype in 1994 as a wheeled reconnaissance and fire support vehicle for France and export, drawing on the AMX-10RC and fitting it with the Leclerc-style FINDERS system and a TML 105 turret carrying the CN-105 G2 gun. After trials in France and Saudi Arabia and a later 120 mm turret, it found no buyers and went to the Musée des Blindés in 2016. In the game it is extremely mobile and has a thermal sight, but protection is weak and ammunition is limited. It was added in its 105 mm form in Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
fury_mk1: The Fury Mk I joined the RAF in May 1931, shortly after the first production aircraft flew in March, and 117 were built; it also served with Yugoslavia, Iran and South Africa and saw combat in Spain's civil war and in the Second World War. In the game it is one of Britain's reserve fighters: it out-turns most biplanes but is slow, climbs modestly and is lightly armed, and it bleeds speed so fast in sustained turns that it has to trade height to stay controllable. It has been available since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
fury_mk2: No earlier RAF fighter had exceeded 200 mph in level flight, and the Mk II of the Hawker Fury, which entered service in 1936, was quicker still; it remained with Fighter Command until January 1939, when Gladiators and Hurricanes took over. In the game it is a British reserve fighter that keeps the Mk I's two 7.7 mm Vickers guns but adds WEP. Slow but pleasant to fly, it can out-turn monoplanes, though tight manoeuvring drains its speed quickly. It has been part of the game since the open beta, prior to Update 1.27.
fw-189a-1: This premium German bomber was never sold directly: it was first handed out in the summer 2016 "Operation S.U.M.M.E.R." event during Update 1.61 "Road to Glory", for 18 pilot Marks of Distinction, and came back in the 2017–18 Special Festive Quest. It now counts as a rare vehicle and can only be obtained through the Gaijin Marketplace.
fw-190a-1: An early member of Focke-Wulf's Fw 190 "Würger" (shrike) family, the Luftwaffe fighter built in over 20,000 examples from 1941 to the war's end for roles from interception to night fighting. In the game it is a boom-and-zoom aircraft with strong high-speed handling, diving and zoom climbs, plus an excellent roll rate. The early Antons up to the A-5 turn better than later versions and can out-turn the likes of the LaGG-3, but turning fights against Spitfires or the A6M2 are best avoided. It arrived in Update 1.39.
fw-190a-4: Produced from July 1942 to March 1943, with 976 built, the A-4 version of the Fw 190 gained a FuG 16Z radio and an engine injection system for brief bursts of extra power, and a tropical variant with filters served in the Mediterranean. In the game it follows the family pattern: it is at its best attacking from above and climbing away, stays responsive beyond 750 km/h, gathers speed readily in a shallow dive and keeps it, but it lacks the agility for dogfighting. It joined the game in Update 1.43.
fw-190a-5: The A-5 moved the Fw 190's engine forward to shift the centre of gravity and raise its load capacity, and from 1942 it served as a fighter, fighter-bomber, night fighter and ground-attack aircraft; the U12 field conversion kit added underwing 20 mm MG 151/20 gun pods for air combat. In the game it climbs and dives very well but turns poorly, and the controls stiffen beyond about 600 km/h. An armoured engine and fuel tanks, 500 cannon rounds and 1,800 machine-gun rounds make it deadly in head-on passes. It arrived in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai", when the A-5 was split into /U12 and /U2 versions.
fw-190a-5_cannons: Added in Update 1.35, this is the four-cannon Fw 190 A-5, backed by an armoured radial engine and protected fuel tanks. Its inner 20 mm guns have 250 rounds each but the outer pair only 90, so putting the wing-root guns on their own key saves the scarce outer rounds. Optional Gr. 21 rockets, adapted from a Nebelwerfer artillery weapon and first used to scatter bomber formations, are slow and inaccurate, but their blast reaches close to 100 m, enough to endanger the pilot at low level. It is a fighter first; bombing is better left to the F-8.
fw-190a-5_japan: This Fw 190 A-5 was lent to the Imperial Japanese Army for evaluation; testers admired its dive but not its agility, ranked it second behind a captured P-51C, and chose not to build it, though Kawasaki drew on its air-cooled engine when creating the Ki-100. In the game it carries four 20 mm cannons with an armoured engine and fuel tanks; the inner guns have 250 rounds each against 90 for the outer pair, so the wing-root guns are worth putting on their own key. It was already present in the open beta, before Update 1.27, first as the A-5/U3 and renamed in Update 1.35.
fw-190a-5_u2: A bomb-carrying version of the Fw 190 A-5, it has been part of the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27. External stores add hitting power but cost weight and drag, which blunts its fighter performance, so dedicated ground attack is better left to the F-8. When bombing, the single 500 kg bomb is the most useful load because the small 50 kg bombs only work with direct hits, and a low release without a fuse delay risks the blast catching the aircraft. Ships are easiest to hit by attacking along their length rather than across it.
fw-190a-8: Produced in more than 6,600 examples and widely used against bomber formations by 1944, the A-8 brought an extra 115-litre fuel tank, heavier guns and GM-1 nitrous oxide injection, which raised power at altitude for about ten minutes. In the game it is arguably the best of the Antons: 13 mm MG 131 machine guns replace the earlier 7.92 mm weapons, and four wing-mounted 20 mm MG 151 cannons share 780 rounds, so long bursts are affordable. It has been flyable since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
fw-190a-8_france: The NC.900 was France's post-war use of Fw 190s left intact at the Cravant quarry, a German repair site whose crews failed to destroy them during the retreat; many were assembled from mixed Focke-Wulf parts. Sabotage and unreliability dogged them, and the Normandie-Niemen pilots who flew them disliked the type, so they were soon withdrawn and mostly scrapped. In the game it is far better: four 20 mm MG 151s and two 13 mm machine guns with plenty of ammunition, a fine roll rate and a structural limit above 900 km/h, offset by weak climb, slow acceleration and turning that needs flaps. It was a 2017 Festive Quest reward in Update 1.75.
fw-190a-8_usa: This Fw 190 A-8 of Jagdgeschwader 4 was flown by Walter Wagner, who was forced down at St. Trond, an airfield in American hands, during Operation Bodenplatte on 1 January 1945; US personnel repaired it, painted it red and test-flew it. In the game it matches the German A-8 except that it cannot carry ordnance, so it is purely a heavily armed gunfighter, recognisable by its red finish and American markings. It was introduced in Update 1.43.
fw-190c: The Fw 190 C was one of several high-altitude projects answering the Allied bombing campaign, pairing a DB 603 engine with a turbocharger under a lengthened fuselage; it tested well and was ordered, but lost out to the Fw 190 D and Ta 152. In the game it flies much like the Doras, weak in turning fights but strong in energy fighting, with a structural limit above 900 km/h, though it compresses at very high speed. Its pair each of 7.92 mm machine guns and 20 mm MG 151 cannons is lighter than other variants' but still effective. It was a 2018 Festive Quest reward in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
fw-190d-12: The "long-nose" Dora series replaced the Anton's radial with a liquid-cooled inverted V12 Jumo 213 and an annular radiator, making it much faster and quicker to climb; the D-12 carried a 30 mm MK 108 in the nose with 20 mm MG 151s in the wings, and only a few were built. In the game it outperforms the D-9 at altitude at the cost of low-level performance, so climbing and diving on targets suits it best; it turns poorly, but its flaps help, with take-off flaps usable up to 700 km/h. It can also carry bombs and dates back to the open beta, before Update 1.27.
fw-190d-13: The last production Dora replaced the D-12's 30 mm hub cannon with a 20 mm MG 151/20 and added two more in the wing roots; built from March 1945 as a pressurised all-weather interceptor with a Jumo 213F-1, MW 50 boost and an autopilot, it reached only about 30 examples. In the game it is fast, climbs well, rolls decently and handles well at speed, with heavy firepower, but it is clumsy at low speed and struggles against later fighters such as the F2G. It has been available since the open beta, prior to Update 1.27.
fw-190d-9: Kurt Tank's "long-nose Dora" tackled the Fw 190 A's poor high-altitude performance by swapping its BMW 801 radial for the Jumo 213, an engine first meant for bombers, producing a fighter that out-ran and out-climbed the A-series at some cost in agility. About 900 D-9s were built between summer 1944 and April 1945, too late to change the course of the air war. In the game it dives fast and holds on to its energy, which suits slashing boom-and-zoom passes, but it is out of its depth at low speed or in long turning fights, and an unremarkable climb often leaves it at a disadvantage. It arrived in Update 1.37.
fw-190d-9_ussr: Over 1,800 D-9s were built, and rather than intercepting bombers as planned, they mostly fought fighters or attacked ground targets; some fell into Soviet hands, and the La-7 beat it in every mock combat Soviet testers staged, though the Dora was flown without MW50 injection. In the game it is a strong energy fighter with an excellent roll rate, climb and top speed, and two nose-mounted 20 mm MG 151s plus two 13.2 mm machine guns hit very hard. It turns badly without flaps, and as a captured aircraft it cannot carry ordnance. It came as a Soviet premium in Update 1.37 and was later taken off sale.
fw-190f-8: The F-8 was the main production model of the Fw 190's ground-attack series, meant to take over from the ageing Ju 87; based on the A-8, it had a strengthened airframe for bombs of up to 1,000 kg, and many of the 6,143 built ended up as low-level interceptors. In the game it counts as a strike aircraft and starts in the air, handy for reaching ground targets or surprising climbing fighters. Versatile rather than specialised, it is less nimble than the A-8, but its 30 mm gun pods can wreck aircraft in a few hits. It has been flyable since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
fw_189c_0: To compete with the Hs 129, Focke-Wulf turned its Fw 189 reconnaissance aircraft into an armoured attacker by replacing the fuselage with an armoured cockpit for the pilot and rear gunner. Two converted prototypes lost the comparison, partly because the crew space was so cramped, and the project was dropped, though three C-0 aircraft had been built by May 1941. In the game it handles fairly well and carries decent armament, but the extra armour makes it slower and less agile than the Fw 189 A it came from. It was introduced in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
fw_190a_5_u14: The U14 kit made the Fw 190 A-5 into a torpedo carrier, with an LT F5b slung under the fuselage, a taller tail wheel and fin so the weapon would clear the ground, and armament cut to two 20 mm MG 151s beside the engine; two aircraft were trialled, and "TD SI" is the one modelled. In the game it flies like any other A-5 and is armed much like the A-5/U2. The torpedo is what sets it apart, though it is useful only in naval battles and a few Air Realistic maps and drags performance down until released. It was sold as a premium from Update "Fire and Ice".
fw_190f_8_hungary: Built from early 1944 on the Fw 190 A-8 airframe, the F-8 ground-attack variant gained more bomb racks, extra armour and a FuG 16 ZS radio, and at least 3,400 were produced. Hungary received 72 F-8, F-9 and G aircraft from November 1944 to counter Soviet armour, yet mostly flew them against Allied bomber raids. In the Italian tree its wide range of stores makes it a capable attacker, while against aircraft it relies on an excellent roll rate, reasonable guns and good speed, short of both pure fighters and pure attackers; unlike the German F-8, it has no X-4 missile. It joined the game in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
fw_200c_1: The first military production Condor had four supercharged BMW 132H engines of over 800 hp and flew anti-shipping missions with KG 40, posing a serious threat until more CAM ships put to sea; crews disliked its thin defensive armament and unprotected fuel system, and eight were lost when the fuselage broke behind the wing on landing. In the game it is a large, heavy bomber that carries a big load at a decent top speed, but it handles poorly and its airframe is rated for only 450 km/h, so diving is risky. Just four 7.92 mm turrets defend it. It arrived in Update 1.47 "Big Guns".
g4m1: Japan's best-known wartime bomber, the G4M was a faster, longer-ranged successor to the G3M that saved weight by skimping on armour and crew protection, earning the nickname "flying lighter"; it took part in sinking the British capital ships Prince of Wales and Repulse (1941) and in raiding Darwin (1942). In the game it carries a heavy load of four 250 kg or twelve 60 kg bombs and is safer hitting pillboxes, tanks, guns and ships than bases, where fighters wait. Its 20 mm defensive cannon is strong but hard to aim, and the other guns are weak. It has been in the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
g5n1: Nakajima's Shinzan was a four-engined heavy bomber for the Imperial Japanese Navy, derived from the Douglas DC-4E airliner that Japan acquired in secret and copied in 1939; it was meant to carry 4,000 kg over 3,000 nautical miles but never entered service because of poor performance and weak, unreliable engines. In the game it is one of Japan's few true heavy bombers, with four Mitsubishi Kasei engines, a 3,200 kg payload and great endurance, but it is among the least manoeuvrable aircraft in the game and is really only suited to destroying bases and other large targets. It was added in Update 1.29.
g8n1: The Renzan was Nakajima's 1943 design for a long-range, land-based Navy bomber intended to reach 590 km/h; it first flew in October 1944, but aluminium shortages and Allied raids meant just seven, four of them prototypes, were completed before cancellation in June 1945. In the game it defends itself unusually well, with six 20 mm Type 99 cannons, plenty of ammunition and armour that is good by Japanese standards, and its four engines improve its chances of getting home. Its 2,400 kg bomb load is the smallest of any heavy bomber in the game, which limits it in ground attack. It arrived in Update 1.29.
g_55s: The G.55S (S for "Silurante", torpedo) was a late-war modification of Fiat's G.55 fighter that could carry a torpedo; a handful were built and used, with no success against ships, and they mostly flew as fighters instead. In the game it is agile with good endurance, comfortable in both turning and energy fights, and three 20 mm MG 151/20 cannons deal with fighters and, with careful aim, heavy bombers. It is fairly tough, but armour is limited to a bulletproof windscreen and an 8 mm seat, so attacking well-defended bombers from behind is unwise. It began as a pre-order pack for Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica" and later returned for Golden Eagles.
g_56: Fiat's G.56 was a G.55 re-engined with the 1,750 hp DB 603, 275 hp more than before, and lightened by dropping the machine guns to leave three 20 mm cannons. Planned in 1942, it was slowed by Allied invasion and bombing; one prototype finished before the 1943 armistice was repainted in German markings, and both examples built remained prototypes. In the game it strikes a good balance of power, firepower and handling for both turning and energy fights, and its airframe takes several hits without breaking up. It came with the first Italian aircraft tree in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
g_lynx: G-LYNX was the Westland Lynx the company kept as a demonstrator and trials aircraft; built in 1978, it toured Europe and the Middle East, and after a 1986 upgrade with Gem 60 engines and BERP rotor blades it set a still-standing helicopter speed record of 400.87 km/h on 11 August 1986. Retired in 1992, it is now restored and displayed at The Helicopter Museum in Weston-super-Mare. In the game it is very agile and carries deadly Hellfire missiles and thermal optics, but its sight zooms poorly for long-range spotting and it is easily brought down. It was a premium pack in Update 1.91 "Night Vision" and later returned for Golden Eagles.
germ_9a33bm3: The Osa-AK (9K33M2) was a mobile Soviet SAM system that improved on the original Osa and entered service in 1975; East Germany received 41 between 1981 and 1985, and after reunification twelve went to Greece and the others were cut up for scrap in the early 2000s. In the German tree it is functionally the same as the Soviet version, able to hit manoeuvring aircraft out to 10 km, steer two missiles onto one target at once and reposition quickly on its wheeled chassis. It is large and unarmoured, and its upward-angled launchers leave it almost unable to engage ground targets. It was added in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
germ_9a35_m: East Germany began receiving the Strela-10M in the early 1980s, when its improved missiles and more accurate guidance strengthened the GDR's army air defence; after reunification in 1990 the systems were withdrawn and disposed of. In the game it rides on the MT-LBU armoured tractor and carries eight infrared-guided missiles for short to medium-range work. The missiles fly well enough to catch manoeuvring targets, and a photocontrast guidance mode lets it lock on from farther away than infrared alone allows. It was introduced in Update "Storm Warning".
germ_a7v: Germany's response to the British tanks of 1916 took its name from the War Ministry department that designed it, Abteilung 7 Verkehrswesen, and used a modified Holt tractor chassis. It fought in the first tank-versus-tank battle at Villers-Bretonneux in 1918 but suffered from mechanical trouble and poor cross-country mobility; of 20 built, only "Mephisto" survives, at the Australian War Memorial. In the game it is slow at 12 km/h and thinly armoured, and its 57 mm Maxim-Nordenfelt has weak penetration and velocity, but an 18-man crew lets it soak up many hits from small guns. It was a 2025 "The Great War!" reward in Update "Hornet's Sting".
germ_amd_35_kwk: After France fell, Germany used captured Panhard AMD.35 armoured cars for reconnaissance, including in Operation Barbarossa, before relegating them to occupation duty; in 1944, 34 were rebuilt with an open-topped turret and the Panzer III's 50 mm L/42 gun, and they fought the Allies after the Normandy landings. In the game it is quick on firm ground and its 50 mm gun can penetrate the tanks it meets, but its turret is slow to traverse and open to the sky, so it works best from carefully chosen positions. It was a 2023 Summer Extreme event reward in Update "La Royale".
germ_amd_35_kwk39: Some of the 34 captured Panhard AMD.35 armoured cars that Germany converted in 1944 received the long 50 mm L/60 gun also used on the Panzer III and the Sd.Kfz. 234/2 "Puma"; they policed occupied areas on both fronts, and survivors went back into French use after the war. In the game it pairs speed and agility with a high-penetration 50 mm gun, but ammunition runs out quickly, and the thin armour leaves it at the mercy of HE shells and aircraft. It was introduced in Update "Hornet's Sting".
germ_begleitpanzer_57: Thyssen-Henschel and Bofors developed the Begleitpanzer 57 without a contract as an escort vehicle able to fight aircraft, helicopters and armour alike, combining a Marder-derived chassis shared with the TAM, a fast-firing Bofors 57 mm L/70 autocannon and an autoloading TOW launcher; shown to the Bundeswehr in November 1977, it drew no interest and was soon dropped. In the game it is fast and hard-hitting, with a cannon that penetrates nearly as well as the ZSU-57-2's and SACLOS TOW missiles for heavier targets. Its armour is thin, heavy machine guns can go through the sides, and the externally mounted gun is easily disabled. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
germ_beutepanzer_mk_iv: With little tank production of its own, Germany captured more than 170 Allied tanks in the First World War, mostly British Mark IVs, and rebuilt them in workshops as Beutepanzer; on "male" tanks the 6-pounders were replaced by 57 mm Maxim-Nordenfelts to ease supply, and Iron Crosses were painted on to prevent friendly fire. In the game it is effective at close range but slow and thinly armoured. Its size and seven widely spread crew make it hard to knock out quickly, though an accurate shot into the rear ammunition, HE shells or bombs can finish it. It was a reward in the 2025 April Fools' "The Great War" event.
germ_bmp_1_ddr: East Germany's army received 1,133 BMP-1s from the Soviet Union and Czechoslovakia during the Cold War; after reunification the Bundeswehr kept them for a short time as the upgraded BMP-1A1 Ost before retiring them in 1994. In the game it matches the Soviet version: it is fast, armed with a 73 mm gun firing HEAT and either the MCLOS 9M14 or SACLOS 9M113 missile, and can kill almost anything if it shoots first. Its armour is so thin that autocannons and heavy machine guns can penetrate even the front, so frequent repositioning is vital. It came to the German tree in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack".
germ_boxer_3105: The Boxer began in 1993 as a Franco-German wheeled APC project that Britain and the Netherlands later joined and France left, and its swappable rear module makes it highly adaptable. The MGS version carries John Cockerill's 3105 turret, first shown at Eurosatory 2016 and the most heavily armed of the Cockerill 3000 family, with a 105 mm high-pressure gun. In the game it pairs a quick-firing, hard-hitting gun with excellent mobility, a hull front that stops sub-calibre autocannon rounds, a turret front largely proof against heavy machine guns, and thermal sights for gunner and commander. It was a 2024 "Mobile Sniper" event reward in Update "Dance of Dragons".
germ_boxer_swatrinf: Germany's heavy infantry weapons carrier, the Schwerer Waffenträger Infanterie, is a Boxer variant chosen to replace the ageing Wiesel; 123 are being built by Rheinmetall Defence Australia under a German-Australian contract, with the first 19 due by the end of 2025 and the last in January 2030. In the game it is a fast wheeled vehicle with a 30 mm cannon that has belts for both aircraft and armour, plus Spike-LR II missiles that can destroy tanks and helicopters at long range. Armour is light, though side-mounted active protection helps, while a small missile supply and large size count against it. It was added in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
germ_embt: KNDS showed the EMBT at Eurosatory 2018 as a stopgap within the Franco-German MGCS effort, mating a Leclerc S1 turret to a Leopard 2A7 hull to prove the two firms could work together; it found no buyers, and the 2022 tank of the same initials was a largely new design. In the game it is a 2A7V hull wearing a Leclerc turret, gaining that tank's autoloader and optics while losing some protection. It can only use French ammunition, and its OFL 120 F1 dart is clearly weaker than the German DM53. It was added in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
germ_erprobungstrager_3_achs_turm: Rheinmetall built this experimental Leopard-based testbed in 1966 to find out whether a turret stabilised in three axes could improve firing accuracy; Bundeswehr trials showed that it worked, but the design was judged too complex and costly and was cancelled. The only prototype is on display at the Bundeswehr Technical Museum in Koblenz. In the game it has strong firepower and good mobility, but light armour leaves it exposed to autocannon fire. It was introduced in Update 2.15 "Wind of Change".
germ_flakpanzer_38t_Gepard: The Flakpanzer 38(t) (Sd.Kfz. 140) put an anti-aircraft gun on the chassis of the Czech-designed Panzer 38(t); 141 were built between November 1943 and February 1944, and it is sometimes wrongly called "Gepard", inviting confusion with the unrelated post-war vehicle. In the game it is versatile, with armour-piercing belts for the mostly light tanks at its rank and high-explosive belts for aircraft. The gunner has no protection at all, so it needs to keep moving and stay near cover. It arrived in Update 1.47 "Big Guns".
germ_flakpanzer_IV_Kugelblitz: The Kugelblitz was the third Flakpanzer IV design, placing a new, fully enclosed oscillating turret with overhead cover on the Panzer IV chassis; Allied bombing prevented mass production. In the game it is highly competitive: its twin 30 mm MK 103/38 cannons fire quickly and accurately, often downing even a bomber with one or two hits, and armour-piercing belts let it destroy ground vehicles too, particularly when it catches a column from the flank. It was introduced in Update 1.43.
germ_flakpanzer_IV_Ostwind: Created in 1944 to replace the Wirbelwind, the Ostwind (Sd.Kfz. 161/3) put a 37 mm FlaK 43 in an open six-sided turret on the Panzer IV chassis, since the gun's heavy smoke ruled out a roof, and it proved useful against light vehicles and minor fortifications as well as aircraft. In the game it has long reach, destructive shells and a quick reload, but only an average rate of fire and poor crew protection. It does best holding fire until aircraft come close, as speculative long shots waste ammunition and give its position away, and it should stay near cover. It was introduced in Update 1.43.
germ_flakpanzer_IV_Ostwind_2: The Ostwind II was an up-gunned Ostwind with two 37 mm FlaK 43 cannons to raise the rate of fire; only one prototype was started, and the war ended before it was complete. In the game the extra firepower helps against the faster aircraft it meets, and its powerful shells can often destroy a plane with one hit. It remains lightly armoured, so ground targets are best left alone unless there is no alternative. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
germ_flakpanzer_IV_Ostwind_2_net: This is a camouflage-netted version of the Ostwind II, a late-war prototype anti-aircraft vehicle on the Panzer IV chassis that, unlike the first Ostwind, carried a pair of 37 mm FlaK 44 cannons; some sources say several were assembled in 1945, but it never reached production. In the game it protects ground forces from aircraft, and one hit from its fast-firing 37 mm guns can take off a wing. Its open turret leaves it exposed to both aircraft and tanks. It was introduced in Update 2.43 "Storm Warning".
germ_flakpanzer_IV_Wirbelwind: The first Flakpanzer IV, the Wirbelwind (Sd.Kfz. 161/4), was the idea of Karl Wilhelm Krause, an officer of the 12th SS Panzer Division, in early summer 1944; it put a quadruple 20 mm Flakvierling 38 in an open nine-sided turret, nicknamed the "biscuit tin", on a Panzer IV chassis and was built mainly by Ostbau Werke in Sagan. In the game it ranks among the best anti-aircraft vehicles of its class, pouring out fragmentation shells that set alight or break up aircraft caught in the stream, and armour-piercing belts handle light vehicles. The turret crew has only thin protection, so strafing aircraft are a real danger. It was introduced in Update 1.43.
germ_flakpanzer_I_ausf_A: Built in 1940 after the Battle of France showed that half-track anti-aircraft vehicles were too poorly protected, the Flakpanzer I replaced the Panzer I's turret with a single 20 mm Flak 38; the top-heavy conversion was badly overloaded and slow, only 24 were made, and all had been lost by the end of Stalingrad in 1943. In the game it is flexible and dangerous, effective in support against ground targets as well as against aircraft that fail to notice it, and its very fast turret traverse lets it react almost instantly. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_flakpanzer_V_Coelian: The Flakpanzer 341, or Coelian, was a 1943 project for a well-armoured anti-aircraft vehicle on the Panther hull, armed in its final form with twin 37 mm Gerät 341 cannons in an enclosed turret; shortages and bombing stalled it in late 1944 with only a wooden turret mock-up built, and it was cancelled in January 1945. In the game the twin guns can struggle to hit the early jets it meets but need only a few hits to bring them down, and strong APHE lets it shred light tanks and exposed flanks. The Panther A hull protects the crew well, though mobility is average. It was introduced in Update 1.43.
germ_flakpanzer_zerstorer_45: To fix the short range of the Wirbelwind's 20 mm guns and the low fire density of the Ostwind's 37 mm, the Ostbau-Sagan workshop was asked in November 1944 to replace the Möbelwagen's gun with four 30 mm MK 103 cannons, and two prototypes were built before the war ended. In the game the quadruple mount is dangerous to aircraft and light armour alike, and the Panzer IV hull is well armoured. The gun platform has no frontal plate, leaving the crew open to machine-gun fire and nearby shell bursts, while raising the side shields leaves it struggling against ground vehicles and aircraft flying low. It arrived in Update 2.35 "Alpha Strike".
germ_flakpz_1a2_Gepard: An upgraded Flakpanzer Gepard with a new fire control system that engages at longer range and reacts faster, plus a pair of Fliegerfaust 2 Stinger missiles on each side of the turret. In the game it plays much like the standard Gepard; the Stingers stretch its reach a little, but aircraft can dodge them fairly easily, so they should not be counted on. It arrived in Update "Apex Predators".
germ_flakpz_I_Gepard: Designed in the 1960s and fielded in the 1970s, the all-weather Gepard puts twin 35 mm Oerlikon KDA cannons, a search radar and a tracking radar on a Leopard 1 chassis, and has long been a mainstay of German and other NATO air defence. In the game its radars let it scan for aircraft and show a lead marker once locked, making it a dependable shield for friendly ground units, though its anti-ground ability is modest. Short bursts at close range work best, saving ammunition, avoiding overheated barrels and giving targets little room to dodge. It came with Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
germ_flarakpz_1: The Franco-German Roland missile, developed from 1963 and fielded from 1977, was a long-serving pillar of NATO air defence, and the FlaRakPz 1 carried it on a Marder hull with radar and optical tracking until retirement in 2005. In the game it is Germany's go-to helicopter hunter: its missiles need no lock before launch, and its IRST can find and track aircraft without setting off their warning receivers. The missiles respond sluggishly, so even modestly agile jets can corkscrew away from them, they do little to armour, and reloading must wait until the previous missile has finished its flight. It arrived in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
germ_flarakrad: The FlaRakRad mounts the Roland air defence system on an 8x8 MAN truck; the Luftwaffe bought 95 in the mid-1980s to protect airfields, 27 of them operated by US forces, and a late-1990s upgrade involving the long-range VT1 missile was left unfinished before the system was retired in 2005. In the game the VT1 lets it reliably hit aircraft out to 12 km, its speed and high g limit catch even manoeuvring targets, and a thermal sight helps in darkness or poor weather. With no gun, practically no armour and a bulky hull, it struggles to find cover that still lets it use its full range. It was added in Update 2.1 "New Power".
germ_garford_putilov: Built for Russian naval infantry, the Garford-Putilov armoured car was captured by Germany in 1917 and given MG08 machine guns, but was only ready for combat on 10 November 1918, a day before the Armistice; the Freikorps later used it against unrest in German cities until it was scrapped after the Treaty of Versailles. In the game it is a truck-based relic, slow and barely protected against rifle-calibre fire. Its 76.2 mm gun has no AP shells, only slow HE and shrapnel that can hurt thin-skinned targets, so it is a support vehicle for picking off weakly armoured enemies. It was a 2025 "The Great War!" reward in Update "Hornet's Sting".
germ_hummel: Alkett's Geschützwagen III/IV chassis, combining Panzer III and IV parts, carried the 150 mm sFH 18 howitzer in the Hummel, built from early 1943 to late 1944 alongside the Nashorn, with over 700 guns and ammunition carriers made; it first saw action in Operation Citadel in summer 1943, and Syria later used ex-French examples in the 1967 Six-Day War. In the game its 150 mm gun can destroy most opponents, but thin armour keeps it off the front line, the open compartment invites air attack, and it reloads slowly with limited gun depression. It was introduced in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
germ_infanterie_kampfpanzer_churchill: Churchills abandoned after the failed Dieppe Raid of August 1942 fell into German hands; evaluators judged the type obsolete, and captured examples were reused as Beutepanzer or in coastal defences. This one is a captured Mk III in German grey with white Wehrmacht markings. In the game it is a strong heavy tank for its rank, with thick frontal armour, a capable 6-pounder, good gun depression, a quick turret and 30 roof-launched smoke grenades for screening wide areas, but it is slow, a big target, and its thin roof is exposed to fighter-bombers and rockets. It arrived in Update 1.55 "Royal Armour".
germ_iris_slm_fcs: This is the radar vehicle of IRIS-T SLM, a medium-range air defence system from Diehl BGT Defence that launches a ground-based development of the IRIS-T air-to-air missile, with a jettisonable nose cap, bigger motor and inertial/GPS navigation with datalink updates; the SLM finished testing in 2022. In the game it directs two launcher vehicles but carries no weapons and only light armour, and the whole system stops working once its radar is lost, so it needs to stay hidden. The missiles combine infrared, inertial and datalink guidance and are agile against most air targets at medium range. It was introduced in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
germ_iris_slm_launcher: One of two truck-mounted launchers in the German IRIS-T SLM, a medium-range system whose missile grew out of the IRIS-T air-to-air weapon under the MEADS programme; a battery normally pairs a radar vehicle with up to four launchers, and the modernised SLM completed testing in 2022. In the game the launchers come free with the TADS radar vehicle and are fired through it, and their missiles mix infrared homing, inertial navigation and datalink updates while staying agile at long range. They cannot engage ground targets, offer little protection against fragments, present a big silhouette and are useless once the TADS is destroyed. It was added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
germ_jaguar_2: From 1983 the Bundeswehr rebuilt 162 of its outdated JPz 4-5 gun-armed tank destroyers as the Raketenjagdpanzer 4 Jaguar 2, removing the 90 mm gun in favour of a roof-mounted TOW launcher and adding hull armour; TOW 2 followed in 1989, and an upgraded Raketenjagdpanzer 3, the Jaguar 1A3, replaced it in 1993. In the game it is small and has a useful reverse gear, but it is poorly protected and its missiles lack the penetration to deal with most enemy vehicles. It was introduced in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
germ_jgdpz_38t: Often wrongly called "Hetzer", the Jagdpanzer 38(t) (Sd.Kfz. 138/2) was a late-war replacement for the thinly protected Marder tank destroyers, built on a modified Panzer 38(t) chassis with steeply sloped front armour and a 75 mm PaK 39 L/48; 2,287 were made in 1944–45. In the game it is low, easy to hide and versatile, with a gun that kills most opponents and a front that resists a fair amount of fire, especially from hills or chokepoints. Its sides yield even to autocannons, so it is vulnerable when isolated and to aircraft. It was among the first vehicles when ground forces opened in Update 1.41.
germ_jgdpz_IV_L48: The first of the Panzer IV-based tank destroyers (Sd.Kfz. 162) was a turretless casemate design built to succeed the StuG III despite opposition from Heinz Guderian; its welded, sloped 80 mm front plates were as effective as over 100 mm of vertical armour, and it carried a 75 mm PaK 39 L/43. In the game its strong front is hard for most opponents to penetrate, so it can lead attacks or hold chokepoints, pairing good protection with an effective gun. Without a turret it is poorly suited to narrow city streets. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_kanonenjagdpanzer: Drawing on the record of wartime Jagdpanzers, the young Bundeswehr ordered a gun-armed tank destroyer to counter Warsaw Pact armour, and Rheinstahl-Hanomag's Kanonenjagdpanzer 4-5 was adopted in 1963, with 770 built; the 90 mm gun version served into the early 1980s, and derivatives lasted until 2003. In the game it resembles the StuGs and wartime Jagdpanzers, but good mobility lets it reach ambush positions quickly, offsetting the lack of a turret. Its 90 mm gun is modest in calibre, yet HEATFS rounds penetrate almost anything it meets. It arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
germ_kpz_70: The KPz-70 was West Germany's half of the joint MBT-70 programme agreed with the United States in 1963; arguments over requirements, notably a conventional gun versus the American Shillelagh launcher, plus rising weight and cost ended the partnership in 1970, and Germany carried the experience into the Leopard 2. In the game it differs from the MBT-70 mainly in a 1,500 hp engine and a 6-second autoloader instead of 7.5 seconds; it is quick and fires 152 mm APFSDS or Shillelagh missiles. Its armour is weaker than Soviet composites at its rank, so it does best striking aggressively before opponents can turn their front to it. It came with Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
germ_kpz_t72m1: The T-72M1 was the last tank supplied to East Germany in the 1980s, a licence-built Warsaw Pact export model that, after local upgrades, matched the Soviet T-72A Mod. 1983 with its extra upper-plate armour; it never saw combat and later passed to the unified German army for evaluation or sale. In the game it plays like the Soviet T-72A, but with the add-on armour included as standard. It lacks the agility of NATO tanks, yet opponents still relying on early APFSDS or APDS will find it hard to deal with. It was introduced in Update "Sky Guardians".
germ_kv_1B_finland: This KV-1E (model 1940) was one of two KV-1s captured by Finland, seized near Petrozavodsk early in the Continuation War and put into service in 1942 as Ps. 272-1, nicknamed "Klimi"; poor visibility, unreliability and a lack of spare parts limited it, it was little used in the Lapland War, and it is now in the Parola Tank Museum. In the game it matches the Soviet KV-1E, with add-on plates, thick front and sides apart from the mantlet and turret cheeks, average mobility, a slow turret and a 76 mm F-32 that hits well with APHEBC and HE. It is rare, offered only occasionally through promotions, events and Warbond shops.
germ_kv_1_kwk_40: Germany pressed roughly 50 to 100 captured KV-1s into service, and the 22nd Panzer Division rebuilt one 1942-model example with a 75 mm KwK 40 L/48, new optics, an MG 34, a Panzer III/IV-style commander's cupola and a T-34 air filter; it was sent to Kursk and its fate is unknown. In the game the German gun fixes the KV-1's biggest weakness, adding strong penetration to the familiar heavy armour and reasonable speed. It still reverses poorly, and the new cupola is a weak spot. It was introduced in Update 1.43.
germ_kv_2_754r: The Kirov Works' KV-2 entered Soviet service in 1940, with 204 built in 1940–41, and Germany repaired and reused at most 10 to 15 captured examples under this designation, adding a Panzer III/IV commander's cupola and using them to bombard Soviet positions around besieged Leningrad; American troops even captured one defending Essen. In the game it is nearly identical to the Soviet KV-2 (1940), bringing huge firepower, good armour and decent mobility. Its reload is very long, the turret turns slowly and the silhouette is extremely tall. It arrived in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
germ_le_kpz_m41: West Germany began receiving the American M41 Walker Bulldog in 1955, making it the Bundeswehr's first post-war tank; it served with reconnaissance and tank destroyer units, gained local upgrades such as smoke launchers, and was retired in 1969. In the game high mobility and hard-hitting APDS make it a capable scout, ambusher and flanker that can reach deep behind enemy lines, and unlike the American M41A1 it has smoke grenade launchers for cover. Its armour is thin and its profile tall. It was introduced in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
germ_leopard_1a5: The Leopard 1A5 came from a 1980 upgrade programme that rebuilt 1,225 Leopard 1A1A1s with a redesigned turret, more ammunition stowed at the turret rear and the EMES 18 fire control system, a relative of the Leopard 2's EMES 15 chosen in 1983; the turret could have taken the 120 mm L/44, but that never happened, and bolt-on Lexan plates were available. In the game it is the final production Leopard 1, and its laser rangefinder and thermal imaging help it spot enemies first and shoot accurately. It was added in Update "New Power".
germ_leopard_2_pt14: In the early 1980s Krauss-Maffei gave its earlier T14 composite-armour turret a nine-round bustle autoloader, cutting the crew to three and allowing up to 15 rounds a minute from the 120 mm Rh120 L/44, and put it on an experimental chassis. Trials found the loader unreliable, the turret top-heavy and the smaller crew unpopular, so it was cancelled, and the prototype is now in a Koblenz museum. In the game it delivers a very fast burst of fire followed by a long refill, so it excels in short fights, while weak armour is offset by excellent mobility. It was a 2021 Export Order event reward.
germ_leopard_2a4: The most widely built Leopard 2, the 2A4 was produced in eight batches from 1985 to 1992, with over 1,800 new tanks, and earlier versions were brought up to the same standard; it added fire and explosion suppression, digital fire control ready for new ammunition and flat titanium/tungsten turret armour, and post-Cold War surplus sales spread it worldwide. In the game its composite armour gives far better protection than the Leopard 1 line without excessive weight, and with the 120 mm Rheinmetall L/44 it balances armour, mobility and firepower. It arrived in Update 1.79 "Project X".
germ_leopard_2a4_pzbtl_123: This Leopard 2A4 represents the tanks of the Bundeswehr's 123rd Tank Battalion, stationed at the Schweppermann barracks near Amberg, which received them in 1990 and kept them until the unit disbanded in 1994. In the game it is fast and mobile, with the 120 mm Rh 120 L/44, blow-out panels and NERA-equipped composite armour, which makes it a sensible first step into the Leopard 2 family. It differs from the tech-tree 2A4 only in lacking the self-entrenching tool and wearing a unique forest camouflage. It was introduced in Update 2.17 "Danger Zone".
germ_leopard_2a4m_can: Seeking a successor to its Leopard C2A1 Mexas with better protection against mines and IEDs, Canada bought 80 Dutch Leopard 2A4s in 2007 and had KMW upgrade 20 to 2A4M CAN standard, with composite armour packages on turret and hull, slat screens at the rear, improved fire control and new thermal and commander's sights; five served in Afghanistan in 2010–11. In the game it keeps the proven Leopard strengths of a 120 mm gun, blow-out panels and good mobility, adds third-generation thermals for gunner and commander, and its hull-side anti-HEAT modules help against shaped charges and ATGMs. It came with Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
germ_leopard_2a4m_can_sm: This is a special edition of Canada's Leopard 2A4M, one of 20 ex-Dutch 2A4s that KMW upgraded from 2009 with extra composite armour, rear slat screens, better fire control and new sights, giving better protection against mines and IEDs than the Leopard C2A1 Mexas it succeeded; five went to Afghanistan. It came from the 2025 Senrai Maidens event and differs from the other premium version only in its look, inspired by the character Elsa. In play it offers a reliable 120 mm gun, blow-out panels, good mobility, third-generation thermals for both gunner and commander, and hull-side modules that help against HEAT and ATGMs.
germ_leopard_2a5: Entering service in 1998, the Leopard 2A5 is recognisable by the wedge-shaped spaced armour over the turret front and forward sides, meant to deflect and wear down kinetic penetrators and set off shaped charges early, along with revised composite armour, spall liners, all-electric turret drives and an independent commander's thermal sight moved behind the hatch; it was also prepared for the later L/55 gun. In the game the wedges make the turret much tougher than the 2A4's, and the commander's thermal sight gives it hunter-killer capability, while the layout otherwise matches the 2A4 apart from minor crew changes. It arrived in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
germ_leopard_2a5_pso: KMW built the Leopard 2 PSO (Peace Support Operations) for urban peacekeeping, starting from the Leopard 2A6EX Demo II with its Euro-Powerpack and 2A5 turret and adding modular armour, stronger belly protection, an FLW 200 remote weapon station and a dozer blade; shown in 2006, it was dropped in favour of upgrading tanks to 2A7 standard. In the game it is a better-protected 2A5, with extra composite armour against HEAT, a roof-mounted heavy machine gun for aircraft and light vehicles, and a 1,600 hp engine that more than offsets the added weight. The weak hull and mantlet and the hull ammunition stowage remain. It arrived in Update 2.29 "Sons of Attila".
germ_leopard_2a5_yt_cup_2019: This Leopard 2A5 was the grand prize of the 2019 YouTube Cup and arrived in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy". The 2A5 standard gave the Leopard 2 modular composite armour upgrades and improved fire control around its Rheinmetall 120 mm smoothbore, and the type went on to see service in Afghanistan. In the game it is quick and powerful, using its mobility to find and engage targets fast, and its mix of protection, firepower and agility lets it fight anything from the T-72 to the T-90 on even terms.
germ_leopard_2a6: Often called the "long" 2A5, the Leopard 2A6 is essentially that tank with the longer 120 mm Rheinmetall L/55, which adds muzzle velocity, range and accuracy and accepts newer, heavier ammunition; sub-variants include the 2A6A1 command tank and the mine-protected 2A6M, 20 of which Canada borrowed for Afghanistan in 2007. In the game the L/55 fires the latest APFSDS, letting it take on the most modern opponents, while its layout and crew positions match the 2A5. It was added in Update "New Power".
germ_leopard_2a7v: The 2A7V ("Verbessert", improved) stemmed from a mid-2010s German decision to grow rather than shrink the Bundeswehr's tank force; it adds modular hull-front armour, better optics and a transmission suited to the extra weight, and the first four went to Panzerbataillon 393 in September 2021, with all 104 ordered now in service. In the game it shares the 2A6's 1,500 hp engine and L/55 gun, but extra hull armour, like the Strv 122A's, greatly improves protection against APFSDS, and third-generation thermals serve commander, gunner and driver. Optional mine protection raises its weight from 64 to about 67 tons at some cost in speed. It arrived in Update 2.33 "Air Superiority".
germ_leopard_2av: The Leopard 2AV (also PT-19 or T19-AV) was a more heavily protected development of the Leopard 2K; two hulls and three turrets went to the United States in 1977 to compete with the XM1 prototypes at Aberdeen Proving Ground, initially armed with the British 105 mm L7A3, and after the trials it gained Rheinmetall's 120 mm gun and evolved into the production Leopard 2. In the game it bridges the Leopard 1 and 2, with good mobility, spaced armour and a 105 mm gun firing strong rounds such as DM33, but it lacks a thermal imager and deals a little less damage than the 2A4. It was a 2022 "Summer Quest" reward.
germ_leopard_2k: After the MBT-70 partnership collapsed in 1970, the Leopard 2K became Germany's urgent Leopard 1 replacement, beating the gun/launcher-armed 2FK in 1971; ten of its 16 prototypes had a 105 mm smoothbore and six a 120 mm, but the 1973 Yom Kippur War renewed faith in armour, weight limits were relaxed and work moved to the 2AV. In the game it is a glass cannon: nearly any contemporary round penetrates it, but its 120 mm gun and rangefinder punch through common opponents' upper plates at long range, a gunner-operated Rh202 20 mm handles light vehicles and aircraft, and about 30 hp/t outpaces nearly every MBT it meets. It came with Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
germ_leopard_2pl: Poland's Leopard 2PL is a deep upgrade of the 2A4s bought from Germany from 2002, planned from 2012 with Rheinmetall and the Polish Armaments Group: it gains electric turret drives and stabilisation, an APU, new thermals, better fire, explosion and mine protection, spall liners and add-on composite modules that make the turret tougher than a 2A5's, though the hull was left alone to save weight and money. In the game it feels much like the 2A4, with a commander's independent thermal sight for hunter-killer play, but the heavier turret noticeably reduces mobility. It was added as a squadron vehicle in Update "Ixwa Strike".
germ_leopard_I: Born from the 1956–57 Standard-Panzer requirement for a 30-tonne tank with 30 hp/t, protection against 20 mm fire and the British L7 105 mm gun, the Leopard 1 entered service in 1965 and, by putting mobility ahead of armour, became one of the defining Cold War tanks, adopted by most European users of American tanks as well as Canada and Australia. In the game it gives up protection for speed and the firepower of the Centurion Mk 10, favouring ambushes followed by a quick exit before the enemy can respond. It has no two-plane stabiliser, so shooting accurately on the move is hard. It arrived in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
germ_leopard_I_a1: The Leopard 1A1 added a Cadillac Gage two-plane stabiliser, the familiar side skirts and a thermal sleeve for the gun, and between 1974 and 1977 the first four batches were brought to 1A1A1 standard with extra Blohm & Voss turret armour; later sub-variants received image-intensifier sights and digital radios. In the game the stabiliser is the key improvement over the original Leopard 1, letting it fire effectively on the move, and APFSDS gives it a firepower edge. It is still a mobile ambusher rather than a brawler, relying on speed instead of armour. It was introduced in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
germ_leopard_a1a1_120: Rheinmetall's private-venture Leopard 1 MPI (Maximum Product Improvement) fitted the 120 mm L/44 smoothbore to Leopard A1A1s in the early 1980s, with a modified mantlet and stowage, then added the Leopard 1A5's EMES 18 fire control in 1985, hoping to attract German and export orders. The upgrade raised the price a great deal without improving combat value much, so nobody bought it. In the game the 120 mm gun penetrates every likely opponent, and a laser rangefinder, gunner's thermal sight and excellent mobility make it a dangerous hunter, but the armour cannot stop many IFV and SPAA autocannons. It arrived in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
germ_leopard_c2_mexas: Canada upgraded about 114 of its 127 Leopard C1s (Leopard 1A3) to C2 standard in 2000 by fitting Leopard 1A5 turrets with a stabilised 105 mm L7A3, thermal imaging and computerised fire control, then in 2006 added MEXAS composite armour kits for Afghanistan, where they stood up well to RPGs and IEDs; the tanks served until 2015. In the game this hybrid of the 1A3 and 1A5 carries extensive add-on armour, but it works mainly against HEAT and does little to stop the APFSDS most tanks fire. It was a reward from the 2020 Operation S.U.M.M.E.R. event, added in Update "Starfighters".
germ_m109g: West Germany bought 586 M109 howitzers in two batches between 1964 and 1972, and Rheinmetall reworked them with a better breech and muzzle brake for longer range, plus German tracks, engine and fire control; from 1966 they gained smoke launchers and an MG3-armed cupola, lasting in this form until 1990, when survivors became M109A3Gs. In the game its 155 mm HE shells can destroy even heavily armoured tanks with one good hit, and proximity fuses let it engage aircraft. It keeps pace with medium tanks and a large crew absorbs some damage, but its armour only stops machine guns and fragments, and the reload is slow. It came with Update 2.31 "Kings of Battle".
germ_m44: The M44 was among the first heavy weapons the United States supplied to the new Bundeswehr, arriving from the late 1950s to support infantry and armour as a key part of the early artillery arm, until the M109 replaced it in 1968. In the game it is compact and mobile, with a 155 mm gun firing M107 HE and M110 smoke shells. The open top and thin armour make it easy prey for vehicles and aircraft, the gun only swings 30 degrees sideways so the hull often has to turn, and the long reload favours fighting at range. It was introduced in Update "Storm Warning".
germ_m55: West Germany received 50 M55 self-propelled howitzers from the US in the mid-1950s as NATO aid, designating them SPzH M55 and using them alongside the M44 until logistical problems saw them replaced by the M110 in 1966. In the game its only real strength is the 203 mm M47 howitzer, whose HE shell carries about 23 kg of TNT equivalent and can destroy any tank with a well-placed hit. With just 10 rounds and a very long reload, each miss leaves its large, thinly armoured hull exposed. It was added in Update "Tusk Force".
germ_marder_1a1: The Marder A1- was a reduced-specification version of the A1+ applied to 350 Marders from 1979 to 1982: it kept the MILAN missiles, dual-feed 20 mm cannon and image-intensifier night sights but went without thermal imaging. In the game it is the first true infantry fighting vehicle in the German tree, balancing mobility, protection and firepower against ground and air targets alike. The MILAN can penetrate most vehicles but flies slowly, so it is safest to use once the 20 mm has disabled a target's gun, tracks or engine, while the cannon alone handles light opponents such as the BMP-1 or M41. It arrived in Update "Red Skies".
germ_marder_1a3: Around 2,100 Marder A1 and A2 vehicles were upgraded to 1A3 standard between 1988 and 1998, gaining armour meant to stop the 30 mm cannon of the BMP-2 then arriving in East Germany, a revised turret and suspension changes to cope with the weight. In the game its high-hardness add-on plates resist autocannon fire at range, though the sides are still thin up close, and the extra weight barely affects mobility. It keeps the MILAN and 20 mm Rh202 but loses the rear MG3A1 and gains DM63 APDS, which penetrates BMP hulls at 500 m and most comparable IFVs, the Warrior aside, within 1,000 m. It came with Update "Direct Hit".
germ_marder_clovis: A Franco-German prototype tank destroyer on the Marder chassis, the CLOVIS followed the DF105 and carried France's better-protected FL-20 turret of 1984, with a 105 mm CN105 G1 gun and a 20 mm CN20 F2 cannon; the cheaper SK-105 and an ageing hull that could no longer resist modern anti-tank weapons left it without buyers. In the game it plays like the DF105: decent HEAT shells destroy most vehicles, a five-second autoloader lets it take on several enemies, and the 20 mm handles low helicopters and light vehicles. It is mobile but thinly armoured, and differs from the French version only in camouflage. It was added in Update 2.45 "Hornet's Sting".
germ_marder_df_105: Thyssen Henschel developed the DF105 in the 1980s purely for export, combining the Marder hull and a strong engine with an oscillating, autoloading turret and CN-105-57 gun like the Austrian SK-105's, but it found no buyers and stayed a prototype. In the game it is lightly armoured, 40 mm at most, and reasonably mobile with 720 hp for 30 tonnes. Its strength is the gun, firing HEAT with 400 mm of penetration on a five-second reload from a 12-round first-stage rack, and the Marder hull still stops heavy machine guns, 20 mm strafing and frontal fire from autocannons like the BTR-80's and Bradley's. It arrived in Update "Winged Lions".
germ_mkpz_m47: The mKPz M47 G is a premium medium tank in the German tree. It first went on sale as a pack in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.", left the store after the 2019 summer sales, briefly returned for Golden Eagles on German Unity Day 2019, and has been sold for Golden Eagles since the 7th Anniversary sale.
germ_mkpz_m48a2c: The M48A2 C was an updated Patton with an 825 hp AVI-1790-8 petrol engine, Allison CD-850-5 transmission, 1,440-litre fuel capacity for 400 km of range, three return rollers instead of five and an M17C rangefinder; alongside the Leopard it formed the core of the West German tank force in the early 1970s, and German examples carried an AEG-Telefunken IR searchlight, rear turret stowage boxes, German smoke launchers and hull mirrors. In the game the new engine and transmission make it more mobile than the M48A1, and decent armour plus a capable 90 mm gun with HEATFS and APCBC suit both frontal and flanking play. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
germ_mkpz_m48a2ga2: By the late 1970s West Germany judged the M48A2 C's 90 mm gun inadequate against Soviet tanks, so around 650 were rebuilt as the M48A2 G A2 with the 105 mm L7A3, a more reliable engine and better optics and fire control, serving with Territorial Army battalions until 1993. In the game it has good armour, reasonable mobility and strong firepower, including DM23 APFSDS that helps at long range and against sloped plates. Without a stabiliser it is harder to use in close fights, so it suits holding capture points or sniping from distance. It was introduced in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
germ_mkpz_super_m48: Krauss-Maffei Wegmann's M48 Super was a 1990s private venture that gave the M48A2 a new powerpack, add-on armour and modern fire control, aimed at the many M48 operators worldwide; the end of the Cold War flooded the market with surplus tanks, and the venture folded. In the game it improves on every part of the M48: a laser rangefinder and thermal sight help the gunner find and hit targets with APFSDS, a stronger engine boosts mobility, and composite screens greatly strengthen the turret, although the hull only gains a few steel plates. It joined the game in Update "Starfighters".
germ_nbfz_VI: The Neubaufahrzeug ("new construction vehicle") was a mid-1930s German multi-turreted tank intended to combine the anti-tank and anti-fortification roles later split between the Panzer III and IV; five were built, and the innocent-sounding name was meant to hide them from Treaty of Versailles restrictions. In the game it carries both a 37 mm KwK 36 and a 75 mm KwK 37 in one turret, and their very different ballistics can make engagements awkward. Despite its size it is thinly armoured and easily penetrated, but its large crew helps it survive hits. It was introduced in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
germ_panther_II: The Panther II (Sd.Kfz. 172) was a wartime project to give the Panther thicker armour, better performance and more firepower while sharing parts with the Tiger II; resources went instead to existing heavy tank production, and it never entered series production. In the game its 88 mm gun penetrates well, it moves like the Panther F, and its hull armour is tougher than any other Panther's. Night vision devices for the commander and driver help in night battles. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_panzerbefelhswagen_IV_ausf_J: This command version of the Panzer IV J (Sd.Kfz. 161/2), produced from March 1944, carried extra Fu 8 and Fu 5 radios with a star aerial, a GG400 generator and observation periscopes, and used mesh Thoma-Schürzen in place of plate skirts; 17 were built new and 88 converted. In the game it plays much like the standard Panzer IV J, including the hand-cranked two-speed turret traverse that makes close-range fights difficult. The mesh skirts can occasionally stop early HEAT rounds, such as those of the M4A3 (105), but should not be relied on. It was introduced in Update 1.43.
germ_panzerbefelhswagen_VI_P: Porsche's VK 45.01 (P) lost the 1941 heavy tank contest to Henschel's Tiger I, partly because its electric drive needed scarce copper, although Porsche had already built ten tanks and 90 chassis; most hulls became Ferdinands, and one tank was up-armoured to the same standard as their command vehicle, serving with Panzerjäger Abteilung 653 from April 1944 until lost that July. In the game a 100 mm plate welded to the hull front makes it tough but slows it to about 30 km/h, while the electric transmission gives a fast reverse for quick repositioning. It suits a push-forward heavy tank role better than the Tiger I. It came with Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
germ_panzerbefelhswagen_jagdpanther: This command version of the Jagdpanther G1 (Sd.Kfz. 173) carried Fu 5 and Fu 2 radios for battalion headquarters directing a company, along with a Zimmerit coating that standard G1s lacked, although it only guarded against magnetic mines that Soviet forces were not using. In the game it matches the standard Jagdpanther: well-rounded, with good speed and an 88 mm that defeats most heavy tanks, though an IS-2 can resist it frontally. Its front is only adequate unless angled, for example behind a low hill, and thin sides and roof leave it exposed even to autocannons. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_panzerjager_1: Germany's first self-propelled anti-tank gun put a captured Czech 47 mm Škoda gun, the 4,7 cm PaK(t), in an open-topped compartment on a turretless Panzer I; 202 were built in 1940–41 and fought in France, North Africa and the Soviet Union, ambushing light tanks well but powerless against heavier ones and prone to breakdowns in Soviet mud and snow, remaining in action until mid-1943. In the game its gun is strong enough for its rank, but the open compartment leaves it vulnerable to HE, artillery and aircraft. It arrived in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
germ_panzerjager_nashorn: The Nashorn grew from Hitler's June 1942 order for an anti-tank gun derived from the 88 mm FlaK 41; with no purpose-built chassis ready, Alkett built a carrier from Panzer III and IV components, shown to Hitler in October 1942, that could take either the 88 mm PaK 43/1 or a 150 mm howitzer. In the game the PaK 43/1, related to the Tiger II's gun, is precise and powerful enough to penetrate anything it meets at long range. Armour is minimal, and poor gun depression makes hilly maps difficult. It came with Update 1.57 "Battle March".
germ_panzerjager_panther: Built on the Panther from 1943 to 1945, with 413 produced, the Jagdpanther was among Germany's most powerful tank destroyers, carrying a fixed 88 mm PaK 43/2 (later PaK 43/3) in a casemate and serving with heavy anti-tank battalions on both fronts, mostly against the Soviets. In the game it is well-rounded, with good speed and a gun that kills most heavy tanks, although an IS-2's front can hold. The frontal armour is only average unless strongly angled, as when hull-down behind a low rise, and the thin sides and roof are vulnerable even to autocannons. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_panzerjager_tiger: The heaviest of Germany's wartime tank destroyers mounted a 12.8 cm gun on a Tiger II hull; built in small numbers in 1944–45, the 71-tonne Jagdtiger had frontal armour on a par with the Maus but the lighter Tiger II's engine, so it was slow and unreliable. In the game the front is extraordinarily tough and the gun overkill, yet it accelerates and turns slowly, struggles in towns where turning exposes its thinner sides, and is vulnerable to chemical rounds that can defeat even its thickest plates. It works best as a second-line sniper or corridor-holder. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_panzerjager_tiger_P_elefant: After disappointing results at Kursk, the surviving Ferdinands were recalled in January 1944, gaining a bow MG, a cupola for the commander, Zimmerit paste and better engine protection; renamed Elefant in May, they fought on until the Battle of Berlin. In the game it matches the Ferdinand apart from those additions: the long 88 mm PaK 43 penetrates anything and the 200 mm front shrugs off most hits, but it is big and slow, and flankers can strike its thin sides or the ammunition in the casemate. At long range it can deny a whole sector to the enemy. It was the Battle Pass Season VII reward in Update "Wind of Change".
germ_panzerjager_tiger_P_ferdinand: When Henschel won the Tiger contest, about 100 Porsche VK 45.01 hulls already built became the Ferdinand, the petrol-electric drive allowing the engines to move forward and free space for a rear casemate with the new 88 mm PaK 43; despite thirsty, unreliable engines, the 91 built were credited with about ten kills per loss. In the game the 88 mm destroys almost anything beyond 1 km and the 200 mm front resists most fire, but the 80 mm casemate cheeks hide ammunition that detonates when hit. Slow and large, it suits sniping or holding chokepoints. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_panzerwerfer_42: The Panzerwerfer 42 auf Maultier (Sd.Kfz. 4/1) was an Opel-built half-track rocket launcher, ordered by Hitler in January 1942 and produced from April 1943 to March 1945, which blanketed Soviet positions with blast, noise and fragments from autumn 1943 and was released to forces in France in May 1944. In the game it can lob rockets over cover to hit hidden enemies at long range or ambush from closer in, but the warheads struggle against heavily armoured targets. Thin armour and a slow-traversing launcher make close fighting difficult. It arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
germ_pz_IV_L70: Vomag's Panzer IV/70(V) (Sd.Kfz. 162/1) was the most numerous of the Panzer IV-based tank destroyers, with about 930 to 940 built from August 1944 to April 1945, and its 75 mm PaK 42 L/70 outranged most Allied tank guns. In the game it is better protected than the Alkett-built Panzer IV/70(A), but as a turretless casemate it suits defensive play: keeping its distance and letting allies take the lead allows it to use the gun's high velocity and penetration on its own terms. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pz_IV_L70_A: In July 1944 Hitler ordered Alkett, maker of the StuG III, to adapt the Jagdpanzer IV superstructure for the 75 mm PaK 42 L/70 to rush the gun to the front; the larger weapon meant extra vertical plates were welded to the Panzer IV chassis, and only 278 were built from August 1944 to March 1945. In the game the gun is among the best of its class, defeating all but the toughest tanks, but frontal protection is inconsistent, so it does best hanging back and choosing its moment. It was introduced in Update 1.41 as a premium pack, returned for Golden Eagles in 2018 and was withdrawn again after the 9th Anniversary Sale.
germ_pzh_2000: Germany's PzH 2000 was developed to replace the M109 after the Panzerhaubitze 70 was cancelled in 1987, entered service in 1998 with 185 delivered by 2003, and has been bought by several countries, including Ukraine from 2022; in 2006 it set a range record of about 56 km with a special shell that stood until 2024. In the game its autoloaded 155 mm fires quickly with excellent ballistics and a laser rangefinder, making it strong at medium and long range, and the chassis reaches positions quickly. Protection is fairly weak, the vehicle is large, and the gun traverses slowly. It was introduced in Update "Storm Warning".
germ_pzkpfw_35t: Škoda's LT vz.35 was Czechoslovakia's most numerous tank, with 434 built by 1939; after the occupation the Wehrmacht took them over as the Pz.35(t), equipping the 1st Light and later 6th Panzer Divisions in Poland, France and the Soviet Union, and passed some to Romania, Slovakia, Bulgaria and Hungary. In the game it is an all-rounder that excels at nothing: mobility trails many light tanks and survivability is middling, but its 37 mm gun is respectable and the front well protected, which suits a role just behind the main push. It arrived in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
germ_pzkpfw_38t_Aufklarungspanzer: The Aufklärungspanzer 38(t) was meant to replace German half-track and wheeled armoured cars that struggled in the harsh conditions of the Eastern Front, scouting ahead of attacks and calling in artillery or air strikes; its Hängelafette turret carried a 20 mm KwK 38 and an MG42 usable against air or ground targets. In the game it handles like a sturdier Panzer II, keeping good mobility and being versatile against both aircraft and ground vehicles, but it lacks the Panzer II's simple vertical stabiliser, and poor gun depression hampers it on rough ground. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_38t_Marder_III: The Marder III (Sd.Kfz. 139) put captured Soviet 76.2 mm field guns, rechambered for PaK 40 ammunition, on the Panzer 38(t) chassis after German anti-tank weapons proved unable to cope with the T-34 and KV-1 met during Operation Barbarossa. In the game the crew has little protection, but the gun is dangerous, making it a good long-range sniper able to crack heavier targets its team cannot handle. It was introduced in Update 1.43.
germ_pzkpfw_38t_Marder_III_ausf_H: The Marder III H (Sd.Kfz. 138) is an open-topped German tank destroyer built on a modified Panzer 38(t) and armed with a powerful 75 mm gun. In the game its APCBC can penetrate almost anything it meets, APCR adds still more penetration, and it is mobile for a German vehicle; the gun shield also wraps further around the sides than on the earlier Marder III. Its weaknesses are thin armour and the open fighting compartment. It was introduced in Update 1.47 "Big Guns".
germ_pzkpfw_38t_ausf_A: The Ausf. A was the first production model of the Czech LT vz.38, and its first 150 were seized at the factory by the Germans in 1939 before delivery; impressed, Germany kept building and improving the type, and it fought in Poland, France and the Balkans before Operation Barbarossa showed it outclassed by Soviet medium and heavy tanks. In the game it is a light tank with armour comparable to many mediums, versatile enough to lead attacks, hold positions or flank. Good gun depression lets it fight hull-down with only the turret exposed. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_38t_ausf_F: The Ausf. F, 250 of which were built between May and October 1941, doubled the armour all round the LT vz.38 design, raising weight to 10.14 tonnes and requiring a stronger front suspension; it served in the Wehrmacht's early campaigns until production ended in late 1941. In the game it faces better-armed and better-protected opponents than the Ausf. A, so its small size and decent gun suit support work and surprise attacks on flanks and rears. The extra armour costs some speed, and its tightly packed crew and components mean a single good hit often destroys it. It was introduced in Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_38t_na: BMM's Pz.38(t) n.A. (neuer Art, "new type") was a heavily reworked 38(t) built to replace the Panzer II, with a 220 hp engine, larger wheels, wider tracks, a lengthened hull, a new turret and partly welded armour; five prototypes were completed by April 1942, but MAN's Luchs won, though the running gear later fed into the Hetzer.
