In the game it represents a late welded prototype with full optics: fast and agile, with a good 37 mm gun and a shoulder stabiliser for firing on the move. The crew is packed tightly and the armour only stops autocannon fire. It arrived in Update "La Royale".
germ_pzkpfw_III_ausf_B: The Panzer III B (Sd.Kfz. 141) was built in small numbers to cure the Ausf. A's unstable suspension, gained a revised cupola hatch, and carried a 37 mm KwK 36 with 121 rounds plus three MG 34s; a shortage of better tanks pushed it into the 1939 invasion of Poland. In the game it is weaker than many tanks at its rank, with light armour that even heavy machine guns can pierce up close and a modest 37 mm gun, so it needs careful handling. It was added in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
germ_pzkpfw_III_ausf_E: The Panzer III E finally replaced the troublesome early suspensions with torsion bars and raised armour to 30 mm, a figure chosen to resist French 25 mm guns, setting the production standard for all later Panzer IIIs. In the game it looks and plays much like the Ausf. B, with the same 37 mm KwK 36, and its 20–30 mm plates are a clear improvement but still vulnerable to nearly every gun at its rank apart from the smallest. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_III_ausf_F: Keeping the Ausf. E's torsion bars, the Panzer III F introduced the 50 mm KwK 38 L/42, and with over 400 built between 1939 and 1941 it was among the most common Panzer IIIs, fighting from the May 1940 invasion of the West onwards. In the game the 50 mm gun lets it trade shots more confidently despite 20–30 mm armour, and the suspension makes it reliable, but the lack of a powered turret traverse punishes overly aggressive play. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_III_ausf_J: From December 1941 some Panzer III Js were refitted with the long 50 mm KwK 39 L/60 in place of the L/42, initially called the J1 and later the Panzer III L, and tanks bound for North Africa also received armoured engine deck vents. In the game the longer gun brings much more firepower and range than the standard J, and an electric turret traverse finally fixes the Panzer III's long-standing weakness. Early T-34s and KV-1s remain serious threats that it can only penetrate up close. It arrived in Update 1.43.
germ_pzkpfw_III_ausf_J_L42: The Panzer III J (the letter I was skipped) resembled the Ausf. G and kept its 50 mm KwK 38 L/42 and 285 hp Maybach engine, but thickened the hull front to 50 mm, with an internal plate taking the turret front to 57 mm in places from spring 1941; a semi-automatic breech allowed up to 20 rounds a minute. In the game it deals readily with opponents at its rank, and the thicker front encourages bolder play, but the unpowered turret traverse is sluggish, a real handicap in towns and on cover-heavy maps where ambushes are likely. It came with Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
germ_pzkpfw_III_ausf_J_td: Twitch viewers of War Thunder broadcasts earned this Panzer III J1, with its own skin, in Update "New Power". It is the first Panzer III with the long 50 mm KwK 39 L/60, which penetrates 102 mm at 100 m, enough for most tanks at its rank, with PzGr 40 APCR reaching 137 mm up close, and it gains an electric turret drive that ends the older variants' slow traverse. In the game it is a mobile flanker for close to medium range rather than a frontline brawler, relying on movement, cover and a quick rate of fire, since its armour cannot take much return fire.
germ_pzkpfw_III_ausf_L: The Panzer III L was built new to J1 standard with the long 50 mm KwK 39 L/60 and 20 mm spaced plates on the turret and hull front, plus a system for passing warm engine coolant to other vehicles; similar spaced armour was also fitted to some older Panzer IIIs, so it is no reliable way to tell variants apart. In the game it plays like the J1, and the spaced plates help against HEAT from tanks such as the M4A3 (105), but the extra protection is not enough for aggressive play, especially against early T-34s and KV-1s. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_III_ausf_M: Ordered in February 1942, the Panzer III M was essentially an Ausf. L with deep-wading equipment, but its 50 mm L/60 was soon outclassed by the T-34 and KV-1, and production ended as resources shifted to the Panzer IV; from May 1943 it gained 5 mm Schürzen around the hull and turret against Soviet anti-tank rifles. In the game, in Dunkelgelb paint, it is the most complete Panzer III, with skirts that help against small guns, but its gun lacks penetration at range, and closing in exposes it to return fire. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_III_ausf_N: The last Panzer III variant appeared in 1943 after attempts to fit the 75 mm KwK 40 failed, taking the short 75 mm KwK 37 with HEAT ammunition instead; extra frontal armour and skirts could not keep out newer anti-tank guns, but around 700 built or converted served to the end of the war in infantry support. In the game the gun reloads very quickly and its HEAT keeps its penetration at any range, while good Panzer III mobility helps close the distance to offset the low shell velocity. Its armour holds up against equals but not against bigger guns. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_II_ausf_C: The Panzer II began in 1934 as a stopgap until the Panzer III and IV were ready, yet served all war; the Ausf. C, built from mid-1938 to early 1940, gained extra 14.5 and 20 mm plates, 50 mm viewports, a periscope cupola and a TZF4/38 sight after the Spanish Civil War exposed its thin armour. In the game its 20 mm KwK 30 L/55 can cripple most poorly armoured early opponents within a single magazine, making it dangerous. It is mobile and has a large crew for its size, but its armour is very thin. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_II_ausf_C_DAK: This Panzer II C represents the Afrika Korps, which fought in North Africa from March 1941 to May 1943; tanks of the 5th Panzer Regiment received enlarged cooling intakes and exhausts and a more powerful radiator fan for the desert heat, though these changes are not modelled. In the game it is a premium identical to the standard Pz.II C apart from its desert paint, and its 20 mm KwK 30 L/55 can disable most early opponents with one magazine. It was handed out at no cost in the 2017 "German Unity Day" event and has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
germ_pzkpfw_II_ausf_C_td: This Panzer II C was a reward for watching Twitch streams in Update "Winged Lions" and can no longer be obtained. The Ausf. C was the third production model, with 364 built between July 1938 and March 1940 after the Spanish Civil War showed earlier armour to be inadequate, and it fought in nearly every theatre. In the game it plays exactly like the regular Pz.II C: its 20 mm L/55 cannon can cripple most early tanks within a magazine, and it is mobile with a large crew for its class, but its armour is very weak.
germ_pzkpfw_II_ausf_F: The Panzer II F (Sd.Kfz. 121) thickened the hull and turret front to 30 mm and added a periscope cupola, a dummy visor to draw fire from the driver and an improved 20 mm KwK 38; 1,004 were built between March 1941 and July 1942, mostly scouting on the Eastern Front. In the game it plays like the Panzer II C but fires noticeably faster and occasionally deflects shells, though its armour cannot be trusted in a duel. Magazine reloads are long, so emptying the clip all at once at close range is risky. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_II_ausf_H: The Pz.Sfl.Ic is a premium light tank in the German tree, originally sold as a pack under the name Pz.Kpfw. II Ausf. H in Update 1.43 and renamed in Update 1.89. It left the store after the May 2021 sale and has since returned temporarily for Golden Eagles during the German Unity Day mini-events of 2021, 2022 and 2023.
germ_pzkpfw_IV_ausf_C: The Panzer IV, developed secretly in the mid-1930s in defiance of the Treaty of Versailles, was the only German medium tank built throughout the war and the backbone of Blitzkrieg; early models such as the Ausf. C carried the short 75 mm KwK 37 L/24 for infantry support, leaving tank fighting to the Panzer III, until the T-34 showed the Panzer IV had more room to grow. In the game it plays a support role like the M8 HMC, lobbing low-velocity shells over low cover, and its armour only stops anti-tank rifles. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_IV_ausf_E: Ordered after the Polish campaign, the Panzer IV E was a lightly modified Ausf. D with a new driver's visor, better-protected hatch hinges, a strengthened commander's cupola with five armoured vision ports, a fume extractor and, from March 1941, a turret stowage bin; about 200 were completed by April 1941. In the game extra protection and new HEAT ammunition let it take on more advanced opponents, but it otherwise plays much like the Panzer IV C. It came with Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
germ_pzkpfw_IV_ausf_F: The Panzer IV F, produced from April 1941, replaced the earlier double-layer front plates with single 50 mm plates and made minor structural improvements, and it was renamed F1 once rearmed versions changed the Panzer IV's role. In the game it differs from the Panzer IV E only in its thicker one-piece hull front, keeping the same short 75 mm KwK 37 L/24 and ammunition, so it plays much like the Panzer IV C. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_IV_ausf_F2: To counter the T-34 and KV-1, Germany began rearming Panzer IV F1s in early 1942 with the long 75 mm KwK 40 L/43, which greatly raised velocity and penetration; these were called F2 until being renamed Panzer IV G in July 1942, and some accounts say about 25 existing F1s were converted. In the game it is the F1 with the new gun, and the step up from the Panzer III's 50 mm to a 75 mm shell means a penetration usually knocks the target out at once. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_IV_ausf_G: The Panzer IV G, in production from 1942, completed the Panzer IV's shift from infantry support to tank fighting, a job previously left to the Panzer III, and helped German divisions against well-armoured opponents in the East and North Africa. In the game it plays like the F2 but with the hull front thickened from 50 to 80 mm, a double-baffle muzzle brake instead of the ball-shaped one, Dunkelgelb paint reflecting its North African debut, and turret smoke launchers for breaking line of sight. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_IV_ausf_H: The Panzer IV H was essentially a G simplified for faster production, and its numbers, firepower and improved armour made it the backbone of the panzer divisions from 1943; it added the slightly longer 75 mm KwK 40 L/48, Zimmerit paste and, from May 1943, 5 mm Schürzen around the hull and turret against Soviet anti-tank rifles. In the game it plays like the F2 and G with a little more firepower, and its skirts can be shot away in combat, as they often were historically. Their weight makes it slightly slower than other variants. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_IV_ausf_J: The last Panzer IV, built only at the Nibelungenwerk in Sankt Valentin from January 1944 to April 1945, was simplified to speed production and save materials, including swapping the powered turret traverse for a two-speed manual one to make room for extra fuel. In the game the loss of the Schürzen and especially the very slow hand-cranked turret make it harder to handle than earlier versions, and it struggles when enemies appear suddenly around corners, so built-up maps are best avoided. It arrived in Update 1.43.
germ_pzkpfw_Maus: Porsche's Maus replaced Krupp's 90-tonne Löwe after Hitler intervened and, at 188 tonnes, was the heaviest tank ever built, so heavy that it needed a snorkel to cross rivers and a special rail wagon; only two prototypes were finished, and the example at Kubinka combines the V1 hull with the V2 turret. In the game it has some of the thickest armour of all but is extremely slow, holding its own against wartime opponents while struggling against later vehicles whose weapons can defeat thick steel, so careful positioning is essential. It joined the tech tree in Update 1.47 "Big Guns" and later became a gift vehicle available for limited periods each year.
germ_pzkpfw_VI_ausf_b_tiger_IIh: Henschel's 1943 successor to the Tiger I paired the long 88 mm KwK43 with sloped frontal armour; 492 were built, held back in service by an overloaded suspension. In the game it is a long-range fighter: the gun is accurate and penetrates well at distance, and the front plate shrugs off many hits from afar, but it turns and accelerates slowly, so flankers are its main threat. It has been in the game since the ground forces beta and lost the "(H)" from its name in Update 2.49.
germ_pzkpfw_VI_ausf_b_tiger_IIh_kwk46: This Tiger II variant swaps the 88 mm for a 10.5 cm gun, giving it far more firepower than any earlier German heavy tank. It sat in the tech tree from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41, until Update 1.91 "Night Vision", when it became a gift vehicle kept only by players who already owned it.
germ_pzkpfw_VI_ausf_b_tiger_IIh_sla: The Tiger II (Sla.16) is a premium Tiger II fitted with an experimental diesel engine, sold as part of a bundle from Update 1.57 "Battle March". The new engine improves its mobility considerably, but otherwise it behaves almost exactly like the tech-tree Tiger II, with premium bonuses on top.
germ_pzkpfw_VI_ausf_b_tiger_IIp: When Porsche's Tiger II hull lost to Henschel's, 50 turrets that Krupp had already built to Porsche's specification went onto the first 50 Tiger IIs in early 1944; their curved front is often wrongly called the "Porsche turret", and the only survivor is at the Bovington Tank Museum. In the game it shares the Tiger II's accurate, hard-hitting long 88 mm and well-sloped hull front, making it a strong long-range tank, but it is sluggish and the early turret has weak spots of its own. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta and was called the Tiger II (P) until Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
germ_pzkpfw_VI_ausf_e_tiger: Henschel built 1,355 Tigers between August 1942 and August 1944, and they fought on every German front; first designated Ausf. H1, the type became the Ausf. E in 1944, and later tanks gained the HL 230 P45 engine from vehicle 251 and a new cupola with an MG 34 mount from vehicle 391. In the game it keeps the earlier Tiger's armour and gun while gaining a slightly stronger engine and a quicker turret, spare track on the lower front plate and a cupola anti-aircraft MG. Its flat armour is still vulnerable, so hull-down positions or angling are important. It arrived in Update 1.47 "Big Guns".
germ_pzkpfw_VI_ausf_h1_tiger: Henschel's VK 45.01 (H) beat Porsche's design, partly because the Porsche's electric drive needed scarce copper, and the early-production Tiger H1 became the first German vehicle armed with the 88 mm KwK 36, derived from the FlaK 36 anti-aircraft gun; experience against French tanks and the British Matilda had shown the need for such a heavily armed and armoured tank. In the game the 88 mm out-penetrates the 75 mm L/43 within about 2.5 km, though not the Panther's L/70, and is more accurate and penetrating at longer ranges, letting it fight almost anything at any distance. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_VI_ausf_h1_tiger_animal_vers: This premium Tiger is a Tiger H1 painted in orange, white and black stripes like the animal itself, often called the "furry Tiger", given as a reward in the 2018 "Flying Serpent, Crouching Tiger" crafting event in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm". It plays like the standard H1, with a powerful 88 mm gun and strong frontal armour but weaker sides and rear, and comes with premium boosters and all modifications unlocked.
germ_pzkpfw_VI_ausf_h1_tiger_east: The Tiger first went into action at Mga near Leningrad on 29 August 1942, where three of four quickly broke down, and at Kursk it was feared because few Soviet tanks could penetrate it until the T-34-85 and IS-2 arrived; Soviet crews were told to close fast and hit its sides, rear or tracks. In the game the Tiger Ost has the H1's 88 mm KwK 36 and heavy-tank speed, while bundles of wood on the sides and spare track on the turret and hull front absorb some hits. Flat, unangled frontal armour remains its weak point. It came with Update 2.43 "Storm Warning".
germ_pzkpfw_VI_ausf_h1_tiger_west: After the Normandy landings, German heavy tank units in France fielded 126 Tigers, which fought mostly alone or in small ambush groups using vegetation, buildings and nets, destroying over 500 Allied tanks by mid-August 1944; at Falaise 105 Tigers were lost, only 38 to Allied action, the rest abandoned or scuttled. In the game the Tiger West is a Tiger H1 in appearance only, with the same 88 mm KwK 36 and typical heavy-tank speed, extra track links for a little added protection, and a full camouflage net that helps it hide in dense foliage. Unangled, its front is easy to penetrate. It arrived in Update 2.43 "Storm Warning".
germ_pzkpfw_VI_tiger_P: Porsche's entry in the 1941 heavy tank contest adapted its VK 30.01 design and used an electric transmission that gave equal speed in both directions; ten tanks and 90 chassis were built before Henschel's Tiger won, partly because the Porsche drive needed scarce copper, and most of the tanks were stripped for parts for the Ferdinand programme. In the game it matches the Tiger H1's armour and gun and is slower on the road, but its high reverse speed lets it pull back or reposition quickly. Weak hull cheeks make angling its hull risky. It was a reward in the 2015 "War Thunder Fulfills Your Wishes!" event.
germ_pzkpfw_V_ausf_a_panther: The second production Panther, built from mid-1943, initially kept many Ausf. D features but introduced a larger mantlet, a cast cupola with an anti-aircraft MG mount, a powered turret traverse and Zimmerit paste against magnetic mines. In the game it is widely counted among the finest medium tanks of the war, balancing mobility, protection and firepower, and its much faster turret than the Panther D helps against enemies that appear suddenly at close range. The cupola MG34 can also deter low-flying aircraft. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_V_ausf_d_panther: The first production Panther, built by M.A.N. from January 1943, improved on the VK 30.02 (M) prototype with an 80 mm upper front plate at 55 degrees, worth roughly 140 mm against head-on fire compared with the Tiger I's flat 100 mm, and 5 mm skirts covering the 40 mm lower sides. In the game that sloped plate shrugs off most return fire while its gun knocks out any opponent at its rank, and it is surprisingly agile for its size, reaching key positions early. The hand-cranked turret is slow, so close fighting in towns is best avoided. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_V_ausf_f_panther: The Panther F centred on Rheinmetall's 1943–44 Schmalturm, a narrower turret with a 120 mm front plate that presented a smaller target, weighed a little less, kept crew space and cut production time by around 30 to 40 per cent; the war ended before series production, with eight hulls and three turrets finished in 1945. In the game the new turret gives much better cheek protection and no shot trap, and it is the first Panther with an optical rangefinder, able to measure ranges beyond 2 km quickly. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_V_ausf_g_panther: The most numerous Panther, with 2,961 of about 6,000 built, the Ausf. G thickened the hull sides against infantry anti-tank weapons while thinning the lower front and belly to save weight, simplified production, redesigned the ventilation and gained exhaust flame dampers; Zimmerit was dropped from September 1944 amid evidence it caused fires and little sign of magnetic mine use. In the game it plays almost exactly like the Panther A with a slightly lower top speed, and its revised mantlet makes penetrating shots into the turret less likely. The cupola MG34 offers some deterrent against low-flying aircraft. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_pzkpfw_V_ersatz_m10: For Operation Watch on the Rhine, the German deception effort before the Battle of the Bulge, Panthers were disguised as American M10 tank destroyers when captured vehicles ran short; the ruse achieved little overall but made Allied troops wary enough of real M10s to cause several friendly-fire incidents. In the game it has the Panther G's armour layout with the Ausf. A's automotive performance, a strong 75 mm KwK 42 and a tough sloped front, but the turret turns slowly and reverse is only 4 km/h, so it should snipe or advance with support, carrying minimal ammunition to protect the side racks. It was a 2017 Festive Quest reward in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
germ_pzkpfw_e_100: The E-100 was the heaviest of Germany's planned standardised Entwicklung tanks, a counterpart to the Maus; Adler began work, but other priorities slowed it, and the Allies found and later scrapped the unfinished hull. In the game it uses the Maus turret on a lower, more compact hull, is more mobile than the Maus though still slow by heavy tank standards, and has side skirts that help against shaped charges and ATGMs, making it formidable with team support. It is one of the hardest tanks in the game to obtain, obtainable only from special tournaments such as "Teutonic Giants" in 2016, and arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
germ_pzsfl_IVa_dickermax: Ordered in 1939 as a mobile bunker-buster for the Maginot Line, the Dicker Max put a 105 mm K18 gun on a Panzer IV E chassis, but the two built were finished in early 1941, after France had fallen, and were sent east to hunt tanks instead, one of them scoring heavily against Soviet armour. In the game its 105 mm can destroy any tank it hits, with its best AP shell penetrating 187 mm, but it is barely armoured and as easy to kill as it is deadly. Panzer IV mobility and excellent gun depression suit striking from cover and then relocating. It arrived in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
germ_pzsflk40_sturer_emil: The Sturer Emil was an experimental anti-fortification gun that mounted the 128 mm K40 L/61, derived from the 12.8 cm FlaK 40, in a large open-topped compartment on a lengthened VK 30.01 (H) chassis left over from Henschel's cancelled heavy tank programme, with an extra road wheel and 15 rounds of ammunition. In the game it works much like the Dicker Max: no real armour, a superb gun and excellent depression for hull-down fighting, but limited traverse makes urban maps awkward. Staying near cover rather than in open ground also helps hide it from aircraft. It came with Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
germ_radpanzer_90: Impressed by foreign wheeled designs like the French AMX-10RC, West Germany asked Daimler-Benz in the early 1980s for a roughly 30-tonne armoured wheeled fighting vehicle; the eight-wheeled prototype, carrying a Leopard 2 prototype turret, was finished in 1986 but fell to budget cuts, though its results fed into the work that produced the Boxer, and it is now in the Koblenz defence collection. In the game it exceeds 100 km/h and carries the 105 mm L7A3 with a range of ammunition, a two-plane stabiliser and a laser rangefinder, making it a dangerous flanker, but it lacks the thermal sights many rivals have. It arrived in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
germ_raketenjagdpanzer_2: The Raketenjagdpanzer line was developed alongside the Kanonenjagdpanzer from 1959, and its variants served the Bundeswehr until 2005; the RakJPz 2 swapped the HS.30 chassis for that of the Kanonenjagdpanzer and carried two roof launchers for MCLOS SS.11 missiles, later replaced by SACLOS HOT. In the game it is quick and responsive, but it cannot fire on the move, so it suits long-range work rather than close fights. Being able to launch from behind cover lets it exploit terrain better than most contemporaries, especially on hilly or open maps. It came with Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
germ_raketenjagdpanzer_2_hot: This development of the RakJPz 2 replaced the manually guided SS.11 with the SACLOS HOT missile; the Raketenjagdpanzers were meant to engage Soviet armour at 1.5 to 3 km, where missiles were thought more accurate than tank guns, and HOT-armed vehicles later upgraded to Jaguar 1A3 standard served until 2005. In the game the HOT simply follows the sight, and the low hull can hide fully behind hills and rocks while firing over them. The missile is not very agile but works at medium to long range, and the launcher has less depression and traverse than on the SS.11 version. It arrived in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
germ_ru251: The Spähpanzer Ru 251 was a 1960s reconnaissance tank derived from the Kanonenjagdpanzer and sharing its 90 mm Rheinmetall BK 90 L/40 gun, intended to replace the M41 Walker Bulldog; prototypes were built in 1963 and 1964, but resources were directed to the Leopard 1 and the project ended. In the game it is a fast, lightly armoured scout whose armour stops heavy machine-gun bursts but little else, so it relies on speed to strike targets of opportunity and move on. It works best at medium range but can adapt to close or long distances. It was introduced in Update 1.67 "Assault".
germ_schutzenpanzer_puma: The Puma is a modern German infantry fighting vehicle, added in Update "Wind of Change". In the game it is large and, for an IFV, heavily armoured, weighing more than a T-72A, yet an engine of over 1,000 hp keeps it mobile; its unmanned turret's 30 mm cannon fires APFSDS and airburst rounds, and the MUSS soft-kill system disrupts incoming ATGMs. It is hard to hide and offers little threat to MBTs from the front, but it shrugs off most IFV and helicopter weapons and punishes them in return.
germ_schutzenpanzer_puma_vjtf: For Germany's contribution to NATO's Very High Readiness Joint Task Force, 40 Pumas were upgraded by 2023 with encrypted and digital communications, data sharing, drone support and a twin Spike LR (MELLS) launcher, with 266 planned for a modernised division by 2027. In the game the VJTF differs from the base Puma mainly in its twin Spike-LR II launcher, giving two missile shots before a reload, while the 30 mm cannon, MG4, armour and mobility are unchanged. It was introduced in Update "Dance of Dragons".
germ_schutzenpanzer_puma_vjtf_mod: This Puma VJTF recreates a vehicle of Panzergrenadierbataillon 33 seen in 2022 exercises, covered in wooden pallets, fabric strips and other improvised camouflage; the VJTF standard itself added Spike-LR missiles and better communications for NATO's rapid-response force, with 40 upgraded by 2023. In the game it differs from the researchable Puma VJTF only in that appearance: it is very mobile with decent composite protection, and its 30 mm cannon and Spike-LR II missiles let it take on heavier vehicles. The cannon's modest rate of fire and the small missile supply are its drawbacks. It was introduced in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
germ_sdkfz_221_s_pz_b_41: The Sd.Kfz. 221 light armoured car, 339 of which were built from 1935 to 1940, scouted for the panzer divisions in Europe, North Africa and the East before giving way to the Sd.Kfz. 222 and Sd.Kfz. 250; some carried the 2.8 cm s.Pz.B. 41 squeeze-bore anti-tank gun. In the game that gun tapers its round from 28 to 20 mm, giving very high velocity and strong penetration for its size, but it only fires APCR, which struggles against steep slopes and does little damage after penetrating. The car is fast but thinly armoured. It was introduced in Update 1.79 "Project X".
germ_sdkfz_222: Designed in 1935 as an improved, cannon-armed Sd.Kfz. 221, the Sd.Kfz. 222 served in every German campaign as a reconnaissance and staff car, doing best on the good roads of the early war; 994 were built, and it lasted until the surrender despite thin armour and poor off-road ability. In the game its 20 mm KwK 38 can bring down even a bomber with a few hits, though the long reload hampers it against small, fast aircraft. AP belts and quick road speed also let it flank and strike like a light tank, though its armour is weak. It arrived in Update "Sky Guardians".
germ_sdkfz_234_1: The Sd.Kfz. 234/1 was a well-armoured reconnaissance car with an open-topped turret holding a 20 mm cannon and an MG42, intended for fighting infantry and light vehicles; about 230 were built from mid-1944 to early 1945. In the game it is essentially the Sd.Kfz. 140/1's turret on a 234/2 chassis, and though less armoured than the 140/1, it gains excellent mobility around the map, letting it ambush unwary opponents with the 20 mm. It was a "Space Race" event reward in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
germ_sdkfz_234_2: The Sd.Kfz. 234/2 "Puma" succeeded the Sd.Kfz. 231–233 series in 1943 as a heavy reconnaissance car, combining the standard 234 chassis with a VK 16.02 "Leopard" turret mounting a 5 cm KwK 39 and an MG 42; about 101 were completed from December 1943 to June 1944, serving mostly in the West, including Normandy and the Bulge. In the game it is very fast and agile, well suited to scouting, but its thin armour leaves it at the mercy of HE, artillery and aircraft. It was added in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
germ_sdkfz_234_2_mod: This Puma wears the markings of the 20th Panzer Division's reconnaissance battalion, which briefly had 16 Sd.Kfz. 234/2s, and is named after the "Biene" lettering on its turret; the 234/2 itself was a 1943 heavy reconnaissance car with a 5 cm KwK 39 in a "Leopard" turret, built in about 101 examples. In the game it plays like the standard Puma, fast, agile and good at scouting but very thinly armoured, and adds a steel helmet on the turret and a camouflage net covering almost the whole vehicle. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
germ_sdkfz_234_2_td: This Puma, marked "Red 18", was a 2021 Twitch Drop for watching Enlisted streams, added in Update "Ixwa Strike". The Sd.Kfz. 234/2 was a heavy reconnaissance car of 1943 combining the 234 chassis with a 5 cm KwK 39 in a "Leopard" turret; about 101 were built, mostly serving on the Western Front. In the game it matches the regular version: quick, nimble and useful for scouting, but very vulnerable to HE, artillery and air attack.
germ_sdkfz_234_3: The Sd.Kfz. 234/3 replaced the turret of earlier 234s with the short 75 mm KwK 37 of early Panzer IVs in an open mount, and 88 were built between June and December 1944 for reconnaissance and infantry support. In the game it relies on speed and agility to ambush, flank and withdraw, since its armour is thin. Its main round is HEAT, which penetrates reasonably but is inaccurate at range, and the coaxial MG42's limited traverse restricts its use. It came with the 2018 "Good Old S.U.M.M.E.R." event in Update 1.79 "Project X".
germ_sdkfz_234_4: Improvised in late 1944 to keep PaK 40s mobile during constant retreats, the Sd.Kfz. 234/4 removed the 234's superstructure and mounted the anti-tank gun with a notched shield, so it could drive into position, fire and reverse away at full speed. In the game its 75 mm PaK 40/3 L/46 destroys most tanks in one hit, it reaches 30 to 40 km/h in either direction for quick relocation, and it can fire on the move if needed. Bushes and shadows help conceal it, and a pintle MG42 covers unarmoured targets and low fliers. It was a 2017 "Operation S.U.M.M.E.R." reward in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
germ_sdkfz_251_10: Of the more than 15,000 Sd.Kfz. 251 half-tracks Hanomag built in many roles, the 251/10 mounted a 37 mm PaK 35/36 to give infantry units and their commanders more firepower; 311 were made in 1942–43 before the weak gun saw them pulled back to rear areas in 1944. On firm ground it moves like a medium tank but trails tracked vehicles off-road. The gun sits above the hull, letting it fire with the vehicle fully hidden, and penetrates enough with a quick reload, but the open compartment and exposed crew make it vulnerable even to machine guns. It was a reward from the 2020 Wargame "Strategist" event in Update "Raining Fire".
germ_sdkfz_251_21: Built late in the war to shield troops from aircraft and support them on the ground, the Sd.Kfz. 251/21 carried a turret with three 15 mm MG 151 cannons and was often deployed in platoons of six, though its ammunition lasted only about 90 seconds of continuous fire; 387 were built. In the game the triple cannons fire fast enough to stop most aircraft it meets, and the half-track chassis repositions well off-road. Thin armour and a long reload leave it exposed to strafing. It arrived in Update 2.3 "Hot Tracks".
germ_sdkfz_251_22: The Sd.Kfz. 251/22 mounted a 75 mm PaK 40 on Hanomag's half-track to boost infantry firepower; factory production began only in December 1944 amid Germany's industrial collapse, though field workshops had been improvising similar conversions since 1943. In the game the PaK 40/3 L/46 is very strong at its rank and penetrates nearly anything from most angles, but the open compartment, thin armour and clumsy half-track handling are clear drawbacks. It was a reward in Battle Pass Season IV, "Fearless Voltigeur".
germ_sdkfz_251_9: The "Stummel" of 1942 reused surplus short 75 mm guns, freed when the Panzer IV and StuG III were rearmed, on the Sd.Kfz. 251 to give infantry direct-fire support; after a new mount and coaxial machine gun fixed its early limitations, it served widely in reconnaissance units on the Eastern Front, proving cheap, reliable and effective against bunkers. In the game it cannot stop even 12.7 mm fire, but its gun and mobility compensate: HEAT with an 870 g charge handles most opponents, though post-penetration damage can disappoint, while APCBC is weaker and slower. It can rush capture points and then ambush from cover. It came with Update "Fire and Ice".
germ_sdkfz_6_2_flak36: The Sd.Kfz. 6/2 mounted a 3.7 cm FlaK 36 on the Sd.Kfz. 6 half-track, mainly to guard Luftwaffe airfields, with ammunition in a trailer and a gun shield only on later vehicles; first tried out in the East in 1941, 339 were built up to 1943. In the game it keeps pace with medium tanks, and its 37 mm gun fires quickly without pausing to reload, enough for any aircraft and some tanks. Apart from the shield it has no armour, so machine guns, and aircraft attacking from the side or rear, are deadly to it. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_sdkfz_9_flak37: The Sd.Kfz. 9 "Famo" was Germany's largest wartime half-track, able to tow 28 tonnes, with about 2,500 built from 1938 to 1944, and in 1940 a few were fitted with the 88 mm FlaK 18 to act as tank destroyers firing from behind friendly units, their crews reasonably shielded from small arms. In the game the 88 mm penetrates almost every tank it meets, but the vehicle is heavy and sluggish, and HE, HEAT, artillery, strafing and even machine guns can finish it, so it suits a patient sniping role from cover and foliage. It was introduced in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
germ_sk105_a2: Austria's SK-105 Kürassier, developed by Saurer and Steyr-Daimler-Puch on an APC chassis with a turret derived from the AMX-13's, a 105 mm gun and two six-round autoloader drums, was built in over 600 examples; the A2 brought better fire control, an improved autoloader and more ammunition. Austria used them in anti-tank and reconnaissance units until 2014, and they still serve in Argentina, Tunisia, Morocco and Brazil. In the game its strong gun and fire control suit long-range tank hunting, with flanking as the fallback in tight spaces, but one hit is often enough to destroy it. It arrived alongside the French version in Update "Ixwa Strike".
germ_sppz2_luchs_a2: Germany's Spähpanzer Luchs, chosen in 1968–71 to replace the M41 in reconnaissance, was a quiet, agile 8x8 with all-wheel steering, a rear-facing second driver, run-flat tyres and NBC protection; 408 were built by 1977, the A2 of 1985 added gunner thermals, and they served until 2009, including in the Balkans. In the game it is not a frontline vehicle: even side shots on medium tanks are a struggle for the 20 mm, and only the front stops heavy machine guns. Its strength is speed in both directions, with the spare driver keeping it mobile if one is lost, though it is weak off-road and cannot pivot. It arrived in Update "Firebirds".
germ_spz_12_3: The SPz 12-3 LGS converted the HS.30, the world's first IFV, by fitting a 106 mm recoilless rifle in the troop compartment for stronger anti-armour firepower; conversions began in 1965, but the troubled HS.30 family, cut from 10,680 ordered to 2,176 built, was largely retired by 1980 in favour of the Marder and Raketenjagdpanzer. In the game its 20 mm MK20-1 and 106 mm M40A1 handle both light and heavy armour, and the recoilless rifle's excellent depression lets it fight from behind low cover. The engine is underpowered and the armour only stops weak autocannons at range. It was a Battle Pass Season XII reward in Update "La Royale".
germ_spz_oerlikon_raketenautomat: Hispano-Suiza's HS.30, adopted in 1959, suffered a weak engine, unreliable running gear and roof-only exits, and a 1960s scandal cut orders from 10,680 to 2,176 before the Marder replaced it in 1971; the sole Zwillings-Raketenautomat Oerlikon 8cm prototype of 1964 fitted it with twin launchers for 81 mm Oerlikon rockets, but the army chose the LARS 1 instead. In the game the rapid-firing rocket launchers hit hard and the vehicle is small, but ammunition is limited, survivability very low and mobility behind most light vehicles. It was introduced in Update "La Royale".
germ_stug_III_ausf_A: The StuG III, the most-produced fully tracked German armoured vehicle and second only to the Sd.Kfz. 251 overall, began with the Ausf. A, which replaced the turret of a modified Panzer III F chassis with a fixed superstructure and a heavier gun for direct infantry support; later versions became tank destroyers. In the game its short 75 mm StuK 37 L/24 lobs HE at fortifications and other targets, ideally from a hull-down position behind low cover. Turning the hull to aim takes practice, but the skill pays off in later German casemates, which pair strong armour with powerful guns. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_stug_III_ausf_F: With German armour and anti-tank weapons outmatched by Soviet tanks in 1941, the StuG III was rearmed for anti-tank work, and the Ausf. F swapped the short 75 mm StuK 37 for the long StuK 40 L/43, creating a cheap, compact and fully enclosed vehicle with a deadly gun. In the game the much better penetration and ballistics let it knock out most tanks at its rank with one well-placed shot, but its frontal hull protection is not enough against the improved guns it now faces. It dates from the ground forces closed beta, before Update 1.41.
germ_stug_III_ausf_G: The most numerous StuG, the Ausf. G was built in about 8,400 examples between December 1942 and April 1945, matching the output of every Panzer IV variant combined, thanks to production spread across MIAG and other plants to dodge Allied bombing and Panzer III lines switching to StuGs. In the game its long 75 mm StuK 40 L/48 matches the Panzer IV H's penetration, the front is strong, and its low, compact shape suits ambushing enemy columns. It was introduced in Update 1.43.
germ_stuh_III_ausf_G: The StuH 42 G (Sd.Kfz. 142/2) looks much like the StuG III G but carries a 10.5 cm howitzer in place of the anti-tank gun. In the game it suits medium to very close range, unlike later StuGs: its slow shells often miss moving tanks, but a hit can cripple the target. The front is mostly 80 mm with some 30 mm weak spots, and the Panzer III chassis gives it good mobility for closing in. It was introduced in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
germ_sturmmorser_sturmtiger: Prompted by street fighting at Stalingrad and doubts that the Brummbär was protected well enough against infantry anti-tank weapons, Alkett converted 18 Tiger I hulls into the Sturmtiger, carrying a 380 mm rocket launcher, from February 1944; it fought in the Warsaw Uprising, the Ardennes Offensive and at Remagen. In the game its huge rocket cripples or destroys anything caught in the blast, but the reload is extremely long and accuracy poor, while the thick armour gives it a chance to line up shots. Its specialised role can make it frustrating to use well. It was unlocked through the 10th Anniversary "Dreams come true" event in Update "Fire and Ice".
germ_sturmpanzer_II: Built on a Panzer II chassis stretched by 60 cm, with a sixth road wheel and 32 cm of extra width to take the 15 cm sIG 33 while staying low, twelve of these assault guns were made in December 1941 and January 1942 and fought in North Africa with heavy infantry gun companies 707 and 708 until the Axis surrender in Tunisia in May 1943. In the game its HE and HEAT shells can cripple or destroy almost any tank, but the slow shells and long reload mean firing only when sure of a hit, and the fully exposed crew is vulnerable to machine guns, artillery and aircraft. It arrived in Update 1.67 "Assault".
germ_sturmpanzer_IV_brummbar: Alkett's Sturmpanzer IV, nicknamed "Brummbär" ("grouch") by Allied intelligence, put a 150 mm gun on the Panzer IV chassis for direct infantry support; 300 were built from March 1943 to May 1945, starting at Kursk and serving in most later major operations against fortifications, troops and armour. In the game its 150 mm, similar to the KV-2 (1939)'s, almost always knocks out a target it hits squarely, and frontal armour of around 100 mm is on a par with a Tiger I's, though the sides and rear are weak. Strong shell drop and a long reload suit short-range ambushes and supported urban fighting. It came with Update 1.61 "Road to Glory".
germ_t_34_747: Germany captured its first T-34s in summer 1941 and fielded more than 300 during the war, mainly on the Eastern Front between 1941 and 1943, some fitted with Panzer III/IV commander's cupolas or converted to other roles such as the Flakpanzer T-34 (r). In the game this composite of T-34 and German parts performs much like the Soviet T-34E STZ: a respectable medium tank with good armour and armament. Its compact interior means one well-placed AP hit can be devastating, and gun depression is poor. It was introduced in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
germ_th_400: Henschel Wehrtechnik planned a private-venture family of 4x4, 6x6 and 8x8 wheeled vehicles in the 1980s, but only the 6x6 TH400 was built; given a 105 mm turret and tested in 1996, it was renamed R400 after Rheinmetall bought Henschel, found no customers, and is now displayed by the Dutch History Survives Foundation with a Leopard 1A5 turret replacing the lost original. In the game it shares the weak armour and survivability of other wheeled vehicles, but has a laser rangefinder, thermal sight and decent mobility. It was a reward from the 2025 "Fast and Dangerous" event.
germ_th_800_bismark: Henschel's TH800 was the heaviest of its TH prototypes at 41 tonnes, entered in an early-1980s South African Army competition for a wheeled fighting vehicle and meant to carry anything from an anti-tank gun to a 155 mm howitzer; it lost to the lighter Rooikat and ended up in the Bloemfontein War Museum. In the game its huge size and unusually thick armour for a wheeled vehicle protect it against autocannons and poorly aimed tank rounds, though it cannot hide easily. It still reaches 86 km/h, and a fully stabilised 105 mm GT-3 handles most opponents. It was a 2020 Operation W.I.N.T.E.R. reward in Update "Hot Tracks".
germ_thyssen_henschel_tam: Argentina needed a Sherman replacement light enough for its many bridges, so in 1974 it commissioned Thyssen-Henschel to design the TAM tank and VCTP IFV on the Marder chassis; the first prototype was finished in 1976, the type entered service in 1983, and the TAMSE plant near Buenos Aires built all 256 before closing in 1995. In the game it is a mobile light tank with decent firepower and thin armour. Its rear-mounted turret places the engine at the front, where it is often the first thing exposed and hit on uneven or urban ground. It was introduced in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
